items.title: Verify email card demo
items.description: A working preview of Verify email card.

items.name: set-new-password
items.title: Set new password
items.description: The second half of a password reset: a new password with live rules, a confirm field that checks on blur, and a choice to sign out other devices.
items.docs: email names the account being reset, as an initials avatar and the address with the middle of the name masked (showFullEmail turns the mask off). The new password shows its rules ticked off live (rules: default at least 12 characters, upper and lower case, a number or a symbol) and the confirm field reports a mismatch when it is left, never on every keystroke. Sign out of all other devices starts ticked (defaultSignOutOthers). The submit button waits until every rule passes and both fields match, but it stays reachable and a line under it says why in words (how many rules are left, type it again, the two need to match), so a grey button is never the only explanation; pressing it early moves the focus to what is missing. onSubmit({ password, signOutOthers }) returns an error message to show above the form, with the field focused and selected, or nothing; a throw shows a general message, and a second submit is ignored while it runs. On success the card becomes a done panel, with the look of the result state but the card's own heading (so the page keeps its h1) and Continue to sign in (onBackToSignIn, which also adds the quiet Back to sign in under the form) and a line about the other devices when they were signed out. defaultDone starts there for a preview; footer, titleAs and labels work as in the other auth cards.

items.title: Set new password demo
items.description: A working preview of Set new password.

items.name: invite-accept-card
items.title: Invite accept card
items.description: A team invite as a card: the workspace, who invited you and as what, a role you can hover for its powers, and one-click join or a short sign-up form.
items.docs: workspace is { name, logo?, members? } and inviter is { name, email?, avatar? }; role is the word, and roleSummary the lines of what that role can do, which become a tooltip on the role chip (on hover, on focus and on a tap) and a hidden description for screen readers, so nobody joins blind. expiresAt says how long the invite stays good (Expires in 5 days, and the date, written with locale and timeZone, default en-US and UTC); pass now for the server HTML and tests, or leave it out and the card reads the clock once after the first paint. Once the date has passed the card says so and names who to ask, with no buttons. mode existing joins with the signed-in address: Join and Decline, plus Not you? (onSwitchAccount). mode new asks for a name and a password with its rules (rules) and calls onAccept({ name, password }); the address the invite went to is fixed in the form, and onSwitchAccount becomes Already have an account? Sign in. onAccept returns an error message or nothing; while either button works the other one waits, and the button that was pressed keeps the focus, so a failed try is one more press away. Once joined the card is finished: the button stays a solid Joined, the fields turn read-only, Decline, Not you? and Sign in stop working and the expiry line goes (it goes after a decline too, and the notice then takes the focus). A long workspace name wraps in the heading and on the Join button instead of stretching the card. Decline (onDecline) asks a small confirmation first. defaultOutcome starts on joined or declined for a preview; footer, titleAs, locale, timeZone and labels as in the other cards.

items.name: invite-accept-card-demo
items.title: Invite accept card demo
items.description: A working preview of Invite accept card.

items.name: sso-sign-in
items.title: SSO sign-in
items.description: Work-email sign-in for companies with single sign-on: the domain finds the identity provider and the button names exactly where you are going.
items.docs: resolveDomain(domain, { signal }) is yours: resolve to { organisation, providers } when single sign-on is set up, to null when it is not, and reject when the lookup itself failed. It runs once the address has a whole domain (acme.io, never acme.i) and the typing has paused for debounceMs (default 450); the answer for a domain the person has already left is thrown out and its signal aborts the request, and a domain is never looked up twice. The field is never disabled, so a slow lookup cannot block typing: a spinner sits inside it, and a status region says politely that a lookup is running and what it found. One provider gives a button that names the company (Continue with Acme SSO) under the company's name; several give tiles to choose from with nothing preselected (each provider can carry its own icon), and the button waits until one is chosen; a long company name wraps on the button instead of stretching the card; no providers gives a notice (No single sign-on is set up for acme.io) with an optional helpHref and the password route (onUsePassword), which is also a quiet button in the other states. onContinue({ domain, providerId }) sends the person on, and its busy state keeps the button in place and in focus, also when the call fails. Enter submits, and pressing Continue before the lookup has run makes it run at once. defaultEmail is looked up as soon as the card appears; footer, titleAs and labels as in the other cards.

items.name: sso-sign-in-demo
items.title: SSO sign-in demo
items.description: A working preview of SSO sign-in.

items.name: reauthenticate-card
items.title: Reauthenticate card
items.description: 'Confirm it is you' before a sensitive action, in a card or a dialog: it names what is about to happen, then takes a password or a passkey.
items.docs: email says who is signed in (an initials avatar, or avatar as an image address) and action what is about to happen, in a few words: Change your email address, Delete this workspace. onConfirm(password) returns an error message or nothing: the message is announced once, against the field, which keeps the focus and empties itself for the next try; counting attempts and locking are the server's job, and the card shows whatever message you return (a throw shows a general one). onPasskey is the second route, Use a passkey instead: you own the WebAuthn call, and a returned message shows above the field. onCancel adds a Cancel button next to Confirm, and grace is the line about how long the answer holds (You will not be asked again for 10 minutes), so people do not feel nagged. The button that was pressed keeps the focus, also when the passkey fails. After success the button shows Confirmed and the card stays still. defaultError starts with a message under the field, for a preview. Inside a dialog, set titleAs to p, give the dialog its own title, drop the frame with className (border-0 shadow-none) and pass titleId if you want aria-labelledby to point at the card's heading.

items.name: reauthenticate-card-demo
items.title: Reauthenticate card demo
items.description: A working preview of Reauthenticate card.

items.name: account-chooser
items.title: Account chooser
items.description: A 'Choose an account' list of the people already known on this device, with 'Use another account' and a remove control per row.
items.docs: accounts is the list of { id, name, email, avatar?, signedIn? }. Every row is one plain button with an avatar, the name, the address and a word for its state, Signed in, or Signed out with a lock so state never rests on colour, and its own menu button beside it, so Tab walks the list and there are no composite-widget keyboard rules. onChoose(account) may return a promise: that row alone shows Signing in and a rejection shows a message above the list. onUseAnother is the row under the list, which stays in view when more than six accounts make the list scroll inside the card (the list then shows half of the next row and a slim scrollbar that is always there, and takes no Tab stop of its own). onRemove(account) adds the menu with Remove from this device: choosing it turns the row into a question (Remove the address from this device?) with Keep focused and Escape to cancel; resolve onRemove and drop the account from accounts, and the focus moves to the next row (or the previous one, or Use another account). In a narrow card the state word drops under the address, so the name keeps the whole row. title, description, titleAs, footer and labels change the words; defaultConfirming opens a question for a preview, without taking the focus.

items.name: account-chooser-demo
items.title: Account chooser demo
items.description: A working preview of Account chooser.

items.name: verification-method-picker
items.title: Verification method picker
items.description: The 'try another way' step of two-step sign-in: authenticator, security key, text message or recovery code, each with a line on what happens.
items.docs: methods is { id, label, description, icon?, unavailableReason? }[]. lastUsed marks one with Last used and chooses it first (value and onValueChange control the choice, defaultValue sets the first one); a method with an unavailableReason stays on the list, disabled, with the reason in text under its name at full contrast rather than faded away with the card. It is a real radio group, so the arrow keys move and choose and skip disabled methods, but choosing never submits: onContinue(id) runs only when Continue is pressed, so a stray keypress can never send a text message. While it runs the button keeps the focus and shows a spinner; a returned message, or a throw, shows above the button and the choice stays. When nothing can be used a notice says so and Continue stays quiet, and a choice that has become unavailable since the card opened counts as no choice. onBack adds a Back button, help sits under Continue (a link to a recovery code, to support), and titleAs and labels as in the other cards.

items.name: authorize-app-card
items.title: Authorize app card
items.description: The OAuth consent screen: which app wants access, as whom, to what, in plain-language scopes, with Allow and Deny as two filled buttons of one size.
items.docs: app is { name, publisher?, verified?, icon?, logo? }: verified is said in words with an icon (Verified, Unverified), and an unverified app also gets a warning, written in the card's own greys with a warning icon (no colour needed). account is { email, name?, avatar? }, with onSwitchAccount for Not you?. scopes are { id, label, description, access: 'read' or 'write', required? }, listed in a Read group and a Write group: a required scope shows a lock and the word Required instead of a checkbox, a write scope carries the word Write as well as its icon, and the whole row is a click target for its checkbox. defaultGranted lists the optional scopes that start ticked (default all of them). onAllow(grantedScopeIds) receives the required ids and the ticked ones; onDeny is a filled button of the same size as Allow and the first of the two in the tab order, never a text link. Both buttons wait while either works, the one pressed shows a spinner and then Allowed or Denied, and a rejection shows a message and loses nothing. redirectHost is named in the footer line, with the reminder that access can be removed in settings. footer, titleAs (the permissions heading sits one level under it) and labels as in the other cards.

items.name: terms-update-gate
items.title: Terms update gate
items.description: A re-consent gate for changed legal text: what changed in plain lines, the full documents, one unticked box, and a Continue that says why it waits.
items.docs: effectiveDate is when the new terms apply (a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp, written with locale and timeZone, default en-US and UTC; a date-only string such as 2026-12-01 is a calendar day and is written as that day in any zone) and versionLabel names the version in a chip. changes is three to five plain sentences, { text, href?, linkLabel? }; an href adds a link after the sentence. documents is the list of { label, href } links to the full text, which open in new tabs so the gate stays where it is. excerpt (any markup) adds a box that scrolls, named by excerptTitle, with its scrollbar always drawn and a ring around the box while it has the keyboard focus. The consent box starts unticked and cannot start any other way. Continue is aria-disabled until it is ticked but stays reachable: pressing it early moves the focus to the box, marks it invalid, and a line under the buttons says why in words. onAccept() records the consent and may return a promise (the button is busy while it runs; a rejection shows a message and keeps the tick). Once it resolves the card shows Thank you, you are all set, says it politely and moves the focus to it, and onAccepted runs acceptedDelay ms later (default 1200), so a screen reader has spoken before the page changes: navigate there, not in onAccept. onDecline() is a button of the same size as Continue, next to a note saying what declining does. defaultDone starts on the accepted state for a preview; footer, titleAs and labels (every word, with {date}) work as in the other auth cards.

items.name: workspace-url-sign-in
items.title: Workspace URL sign-in
items.description: Sign in to a workspace by its address: your domain after the name, recent workspaces that skip the typing, and a way to find a forgotten one.
items.docs: domain is your product's domain, written after the field as .example.com. The field cleans what is typed or pasted: lower case, no spaces, only letters, digits and hyphens, and a whole address such as https://Acme.example.com/login leaves acme (cleanWorkspaceSlug is exported from workspace-url-sign-in/slug). Enter submits. onContinue(slug) returns an error message or nothing: a message (it may contain {address}, filled with the address that was tried, acme.example.com) is announced against the field, which keeps the value, selects it and takes the focus; nothing means go, and that is where you navigate. A throw shows a general message. recent is { slug, name, logo? }[]: each row is a button that skips the typing and shows busy while it opens; in a card narrower than 22rem the hover arrow of a row is dropped, so the address has the room. onRemoveRecent adds a remove button per row that turns the row into a question (Remove Northwind Studio from this device?) with Keep focused and Escape to cancel; resolve and drop the item from recent and the focus moves to the next row. onFindWorkspace adds Forgot your workspace address? for an email lookup. defaultSlug, defaultError and defaultConfirming set the start for previews; footer, titleAs and labels work as in the other auth cards.

items.name: phone-sign-in
items.title: Phone sign-in
items.description: Sign in with a phone number: a country code and number checked on blur, a text with a code, then six boxes with resend and a way to change the number.
items.docs: onRequestCode(phone) receives the number in the international form, +31612345678 (the phone field's own output), and resolves whether or not the number has an account; reject only when the request itself failed. The first step catches a number that cannot be right when the field is left and again on submit, with the shape it should have in words (Enter a Dutch number: 9 digits after +31, like 6 12 34 56 78 for the eight countries of the field, a length rule for any other); phoneProblem and formatPhone are exported from phone-sign-in/phone. Step two shows the number as +31 6 12 34 56 78 with Change number (which also stops the resend wait and clears what was last said), and codeLength boxes (default 6): the first asks the phone to offer the code from the message, pasting fills them all, and the last digit calls onVerify(code), which resolves true (sign in and navigate) or false: a wrong code is announced once, the boxes are cleared and the first has the focus. Resend code waits resendAfter seconds (default 30), counting down in tabular figures from timestamps, and speaks only when the wait starts and when it ends. smsNotice is the optional line about message rates, onUseEmail adds Use email instead, defaultCountry and countries go to the phone field. defaultPhone, defaultSent, defaultError and defaultCodeError set the start for previews; footer, titleAs and labels work as in the other auth cards.

items.name: device-code-entry
items.title: Device code entry
items.description: The page behind a CLI or TV login: type the short code from the device, check which device it is, then approve or deny.
items.docs: onSubmitCode(code) receives the code as the device shows it, in groups (WDJB-MJHT), and returns { deviceName, location?, requestedAt? } to move on, or a string for a code that is wrong or expired, which is announced and leaves the code in the boxes for correcting; a throw shows a general message. The boxes take only the characters of alphabet (default twenty consonants, so O and 0 can never be confused; cleanDeviceCode and formatDeviceCode are exported from device-code-entry/code): letters are upper-cased as typed, a character outside the alphabet is stopped before it lands and named in a polite line, and pasting works in any case, with or without the hyphen. codeLength (default 8) and groupAfter (default 4) shape the boxes. Step two asks Connect {client} on {device}? (clientName and account are yours) with the device, its approximate location, when it asked (written with locale and timeZone, with the zone's name after the time) and the code as facts, the line Only continue if you started this on your own device, and Approve and Deny as two buttons of one size; onApprove and onDeny may return promises, and the answer is shown and announced. defaultCode, defaultError, defaultRequest and defaultOutcome set the start for previews; locale, timeZone, footer, titleAs and labels work as in the other auth cards.

items.name: pin-lock-screen
items.title: PIN lock screen
items.description: A locked-session screen with a numeric keypad: avatar, dots that fill as digits land, a shake on a wrong PIN and a way out to sign out.
items.docs: user is { name, image?, detail? }; lockedAt (written as a clock time with locale and timeZone) and length (default 4) shape the screen. The keypad is a plain grid of buttons; the number row, Backspace and Escape work too, a held key does not repeat, and keyboard={false} turns the listener off. The dots are drawn only: a polite status says 3 of 4 digits entered, and the digits themselves are never written into the page. When the last digit lands onUnlock(pin) runs and resolves true (unlock) or false: the dots turn red and shake once (not under reduced motion), the PIN clears and Wrong PIN, 2 tries left is announced from attemptsLeft, which you count. With attemptsLeft at 0 the keys stop and Sign out is the way on. busy holds the keys while something of yours checks; onForgot and onSignOut add the two buttons. defaultWrong starts with the wrong-PIN message for a preview; titleAs and labels work as in the other auth cards. The screen fills the viewport (min-h-dvh), and the rhs-pin-shake keyframes are added to your CSS with it.

items.name: relative-time
items.title: Relative time
items.description: A time element that reads '5 minutes ago', keeps itself current without ticking, and shows the exact date, time and zone in a tooltip.
items.docs: value is the moment (a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp). The words are cut, never rounded up: 59 minutes never reads 1 hour, and yesterday is the previous calendar day in timeZone, not 24 hours ago. After threshold days (default 7; Infinity never, 0 always) the words give way to a date written by format (short, medium, long, datetime, or your own Intl options). The text is rewritten at the moments it changes, with one timer that waits for the next change instead of ticking; updateEvery (seconds, default 60) is the longest it goes without a check and 0 reads the clock once. Nothing runs while the tab is hidden and nothing is announced. now pins the clock for tests, previews and words in server HTML; without it the server and the first paint write the date with its year and the words take over once the browser's clock is known. The exact moment sits in datetime, in a tooltip that hover, tap and (with focusable) keyboard focus open, and in text for screen readers; tooltip={false} leaves it in the title. justNow words a time under a minute. relative-time/format exports the same functions (relativeText, dateText, exactText) for a Server Component.

items.name: expandable-text
items.title: Expandable text
items.description: Long text folded to a few lines, with a Show more toggle that appears only when something is actually hidden and moves the height.
items.docs: children is the text; lines (default 3) is how many lines show folded. The text is measured with a ResizeObserver against the height of those lines, again on resize, on a text change and when a web font arrives, so the toggle exists only while something is cut. In the browser the first measure runs before the first paint, so a client render never shows the toggle late; in server-rendered HTML it appears once the page is live. The whole text is always in the DOM and folded by CSS (a line clamp), so search, translation and screen readers have all of it; the toggle has aria-expanded and aria-controls. Controlled with expanded and onExpandedChange, or uncontrolled with defaultExpanded. moreLabel and lessLabel are the words on the toggle. The height moves over 200ms with the ellipsis switched off for that time, and snaps under reduced motion. textClassName styles the paragraph, className the wrapper; the line height must be a real length (leading-relaxed, not normal).

items.name: priority-indicator
items.title: Priority indicator
items.description: Priority as a drawn mark and a word: urgent, high, medium, low or none, readable without colour, and optionally a menu to change it.
items.docs: priority is urgent, high, medium, low or none. Low, medium and high are three ascending bars with 1, 2 and 3 filled; urgent is a filled square with an exclamation mark cut out of it; none is three flat dashes. Each level has its own shape, so it reads in one colour and without colour vision, and the word is real text. size is sm (14px mark, 12px type), md (16px, 14px) or lg (20px, 16px) on one 16 unit grid. showLabel={false} keeps the mark alone, with the word in a tooltip and in the text a screen reader hears (Priority: High). editable makes it a button that opens a menu of the five levels; onPriorityChange receives the choice and the mark follows the priority you pass, so the value stays yours. labels translates the five words, label is the noun a screen reader hears first and menuLabel the menu heading. PriorityGlyph, PRIORITIES and PRIORITY_WORDS are exported from priority-indicator/glyph for a Server Component or a table cell of your own.

items.name: testimonial-card
items.title: Testimonial card
items.description: One customer quote as a card: the words, the person with a portrait or initials, their role and an optional rating written in words.
items.docs: quote and author ({ name, role?, company?, image? }) are all it needs. It renders a figure with the quote in a blockquote and the person in its figcaption, so the attribution belongs to the quote. rating (0 to ratingMax, default 5, halves allowed) draws stars and is written in words for screen readers (Rated 5 out of 5, translated with labels.rated). A quote longer than lines (6, or 7 when featured) folds with a Read more toggle. href makes the name a link whose target covers the card, with the toggle staying a button on top of it. featured sets one quote larger on a tinted surface. The card has no margin and no width of its own, fills the height of its grid cell and pins the person to the bottom, so it drops into grids, carousels and marquees as it is. It is a Server Component.

items.name: article-card
items.title: Article card
items.description: A post or article preview as a single link: cover, topic, date, headline, summary, author and reading time, vertical or horizontal.
items.docs: href, title, excerpt, image ({ src, alt?, width?, height?, placeholder? }), category, author ({ name, image? }), date, readingTime and orientation. The headline is the link and its target stretches over the whole card, so a click anywhere on it opens the article (the text on it cannot be selected by dragging) and the focus ring goes around the whole card. The cover is boxed in a fixed shape (aspect, default 1.6) from the first paint, with a blurred placeholder behind it (a tiny data URL, the way Next.js hands one over), so a list never jumps while pictures arrive; media replaces the plain img with your own element, such as next/image with fill. The headline is cut to two lines and the summary to three, and the author sits at the bottom, so cards of different lengths line up in a grid. date becomes a time element written with locale and timeZone (default en-US and UTC; a date-only string such as 2026-10-14 is a calendar day, written as that day in any zone and kept as it is in datetime). orientation horizontal puts the picture beside the text once the card itself is 40rem wide, by container query, and stacks it in a narrower one. titleAs sets the heading element. It is a Server Component.

items.name: commit-list
items.title: Commit list
items.description: Commits grouped by day under sticky headings: subject link, author, time in words, CI status as a glyph and word, and a short hash that copies.
items.docs: commits is { hash, message, body?, author: { name, image? }, committedAt, status?, merge?, href? }[], newest first, and they are grouped by calendar day in timeZone (default UTC) under headings that stick while their commits scroll past; set --commit-list-top on the list to park them under a fixed header. The first line of message is the subject: with href it is a link, without one but with onSelect a button. onSelect(commit, event) runs on both, so a client-side router can call event.preventDefault(). Whatever follows the first line of message (or body) folds behind a disclosure button. status is success, failure, running, pending or cancelled and is always a glyph plus a word (labels.statuses to translate). The short hash copies the full hash. Times are words (3 minutes ago, yesterday) with the exact moment in a tooltip that a tap opens too; pass now to pin the clock for server HTML and tests, otherwise the list reads the browser clock after the first paint and writes the full date until then. The row lays itself out by the width of the list, not of the window, so it also works in a narrow column.

items.name: appointment-card
items.title: Appointment card
items.description: An upcoming appointment at a glance: a date leaf, the time and its length, who and where, a status badge, and actions to reschedule, cancel or add to a calendar.
items.docs: start and end are exact moments (a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string with its offset); timeZone is where the appointment takes place and every time on the card is written in it (Thu, Nov 5, 2026 and 10:00 AM – 10:45 AM · 45 min). readerTimeZone is the zone of the person looking: when its clock tells another time the card names the zone (10:00 – 10:45 GMT-5), and without it the card reads the browser zone after the first paint. status is confirmed, pending or cancelled; an appointment whose end has passed (against now, or the browser clock) mutes and says Completed (Expired when it was never confirmed). location.url makes it an Online appointment with a Join video call link while it is still to come, location.address an On site one. actions: onReschedule adds a button; onCancel adds a Cancel appointment entry in a menu that asks first in a dialog whose safe answer has the focus, shows a busy state while your promise runs and stays open with a message when it rejects, and once it resolves the card shows itself cancelled; calendar (default true) adds Add to calendar built from the appointment. labels carries every word, with {title}, {person} and {date} filled in.

items.name: company-card
items.title: Company card
items.description: A company at a glance for CRMs and directories: logo, name, domain, status, and facts for industry, size, place, owner and last contact.
items.docs: name is the one primary link of the card (href, or onOpen for a button); the whole card opens it. domain is the website, with or without the scheme and the path (https://www.halcyon-freight.com/about shows halcyon-freight.com) and opens in a new tab, with that said in the link for screen readers. The logo is an image address; without one, or while it loads, the card shows the initials of the name. size is a number (written 240 employees) or your own words. owner is { name, image? }. lastContact is a date written in words (3 days ago, yesterday) with the exact date in a tooltip a tap opens too; null says Not contacted yet and leaving it out shows no line. status is lead, prospect, customer or lost: a badge with its own glyph, weight and word. Facts you leave out leave no empty row. Pass now to pin the clock for server HTML and tests; otherwise the card reads the browser clock after the first paint and writes the date until then. labels carries every word.

items.name: invitation-card
items.title: Invitation card
items.description: An invitation you received: who sent it, what to and as which role, with Accept and Decline of equal weight and the outcome in words afterwards.
items.docs: inviter is { name, image? }, target is { name, type, image?, href? } (type is the kind of thing in lower case, workspace or project or team, and is written into the words) and role is the role in words. state is controlled (pending, accepted, declined or expired) with onStateChange, or leave it out and the card moves itself once your callbacks resolve; defaultState starts it elsewhere. Pending shows Accept and Decline as two buttons of the same size and style, a glyph each: while onAccept or onDecline runs neither answers a second press (both are aria-disabled, so the keyboard stays on the button that was pressed) and the pressed one is busy, and a rejection keeps the card pending and says so. Once a decision is made the keyboard moves to the outcome, so nobody has to Tab back from the top of the page. Accepted states the outcome and links to target.href (Open workspace). Declined says so and offers Undo for undoSeconds (default 10, 0 turns it off) through onUndo. expiresAt shows Expires in 5 days with the date; once it has passed, against now or the browser clock, the card shows itself expired whatever state says, explains why and offers Ask for a new invite when onRequestNew is given. Pass now to pin the clock for server HTML and tests. labels carries every word, with {inviter}, {role}, {target} and {type} filled in.

items.name: api-endpoint
items.title: API endpoint
items.description: An API route as one row: the method as a label told apart by weight and outline, the path with its parameters quieter, a line on what it does and the auth it needs.
items.docs: method is GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, drawn as a label in monospace whose fill, outline (thin, heavy or dashed) and weight tell the five apart in black and white (only DELETE borrows the destructive token). path is the route with its parameters written :id or {id} (a query string works too): fixed parts are set in a medium weight and the parameters in a quieter one, so the shape of the route reads at a glance. baseUrl is what the routes hang from; the copy button copies baseUrl + path, so the clipboard holds an address that works in a terminal (fullUrl and routeParts are exported if you need them). auth is the words (Bearer token, API key, OAuth 2 · orders:read), false says it needs nothing and leaving it out says nothing; screen readers hear Authentication: before it. deprecated strikes the route through and adds a Deprecated mark. With href the route is the row's one link and the whole row opens it, while the copy button stays a separate target. Every link and copy button names its route (GET /v1/orders, Copy URL of GET /v1/orders), so a screen reader listing them can tell the routes apart. A Server Component; labels carries the words, and labels.copy takes {method} and {path}.

items.name: repo-card
items.title: Repo card
items.description: A code repository as a card: owner and name as one link, description, topics, language, stars, forks and when it last changed.
items.docs: name is the one link of the card (href, or onOpen for a button) and owner is written before it in a quieter weight; the whole card opens the repository, while the counts and the date stay separate targets above it. language is words beside a small neutral marker, never a brand colour. stars and forks are written short (12.4K) in the locale's own way and say the full number (12,384 stars) in a tooltip, which a tap opens too, and to screen readers. updatedAt is written in words (3 days ago) with the exact date in a tooltip; pass now to pin the clock for server HTML and tests, otherwise the card reads the browser clock after the first paint and writes the date until then. visibility is public or private, a badge with a glyph and the word. topics are tags, maxTopics (default 4) of them before +N, which screen readers hear as 3 more topics. labels carries every word, with {count} and {time} filled in.

items.name: experience-list
items.title: Experience list
items.description: A CV section: roles with organisation, dates and duration, a few lines on what was done and skills as tags, in a two-column rhythm that stacks on a phone.
items.docs: entries is { role, organisation, logo?, start, end?, location?, bullets?, skills? }[], newest first, drawn as an ordered list of articles, each with a heading (the role; headingLevel sets it). Dates sit in a left column, written in months (Mar 2022 – Present) with how long it lasted under them, and move above the details on a phone. A start or end such as 2022-03 is a month and 2022-03-14 a calendar day: neither shifts with timeZone, and a month given as the end counts as worked through, so Jan 2019 to Mar 2023 is 4 yrs 3 mos. A role without an end says Present in words and is measured to now; leave now out to use the browser clock, which the list reads after the first paint (until then the length of a current role is left out, so server and browser agree). Entries with the same organisation next to each other group under one heading with the time at the organisation added up and the roles on a thin timeline. variant education writes years only and no lengths. labels carries the words, with {count} filled in.

items.name: job-card
items.title: Job card
items.description: A job opening as one card: company, title, a labelled list of place, mode, contract and pay, skill tags, how fresh it is, and a save toggle.
items.docs: title is the one link of the card (href, or onOpen for a button; a screen reader also hears at {company}) and the whole card opens it. location, workMode (onsite, hybrid or remote) and type are facts in a definition list with a glyph each, and salary is { min?, max?, currency, period? } formatted with Intl in the locale you name: 85000 to 105000 EUR per year reads €85K – €105K / year (a range is written in one style: from 10,000 up both ends are short, 9500 to 12500 reads €9.5K – €12.5K), with a minimum only From €85K, with a maximum only Up to €105K, and with no salary there is no pay row at all. postedAt is written in words (Posted 2 days ago) with the exact date in a tooltip a tap opens too, and a posting under three days old gets New in words; pass now to pin the clock for server HTML and tests, otherwise the card reads the browser clock after the first paint. The save button is a toggle with aria-pressed whose name says which job it saves (Save Senior Product Designer at Halcyon Freight); saved controls it (or defaultSaved lets the card keep it), onSave(next) reports it, and it is a separate target above the card's link. labels carries every word.

items.name: property-card
items.title: Property card
items.description: A home listing as a card: a gallery of photos with arrows, the price in tabular numerals, the address, bedrooms, bathrooms and area with units, a status and a save toggle.
items.docs: images is { src, alt }[]: the first is on show, they scroll with native snapping (swipe, trackpad) or with the two arrows, which loop and appear on hover and focus, and a counter says which photo you are on; from the keyboard the gallery itself is one tab stop and the left and right arrow keys step through it (the arrow buttons are for the pointer and for screen readers); one photo has no arrows and none shows a quiet placeholder. Every photo needs an alt, which is what the gallery reads out. price is a number written in currency (default EUR) and locale as tabular numerals with no cents, or your own words (€2,150 / month). facts is { beds, baths, area, plot } and is written with its units as a labelled list (3 beds, 2 baths, 142 m², 310 m² plot): for square feet set labels.area to {count} sq ft. status is for-sale, under-offer, sold or new, a badge in a word on the first photo; a sold listing is muted (black and white photos, a quiet price). The address is the one link of the card (href, or onOpen for a button) and a tap or click on a photo opens it too, while the arrows and the heart are separate targets above it. The heart is a toggle with aria-pressed whose name carries the address (Save Prinsengracht 214, Amsterdam): saved controls it (or defaultSaved lets the card keep it) and onSave(next) reports it. labels carries every word.

items.name: amenity-list
items.title: Amenity list
items.description: What a place offers as an icon grid of amenities, sorted under headings, with a 'Show all 24 amenities' toggle for the long tail.
items.docs: amenities is { id, label, icon?, available?, note?, group? }[]: icon is an element drawn at 20px (<IconWifi />), and without one the item shows a check. An amenity with available: false is struck through, says Not included to the eye and, as hidden text, to a screen reader, and keeps its note after it. The first visibleCount (default 8, in reading order) show; the rest sit behind a toggle that says how many there are in all (Show all 24 amenities) and reports aria-expanded and aria-controls. With no more than visibleCount items there is no toggle. groups is { id, label }[]: the amenities are sorted under those headings in that order, a heading is drawn as soon as one of its items shows, and amenities whose group is missing or unknown go under Other. expanded (or defaultExpanded) and onExpandedChange control the toggle. labels carries every word, with {count} filled in.

items.name: curriculum-list
items.title: Curriculum list
items.description: A course outline: modules that fold open to lessons with type, length and state, so learners see what is done, current, locked or free to preview.
items.docs: modules is { id, title, lessons }[] and each lesson { id, title, type (video, reading or quiz), minutes?, state?, href?, reason? }. A module header says how far the learner is (3 of 5 lessons, counted from lessons whose state is completed) and how long the module takes in all, with a thin bar that shows it. current is the id of the lesson the learner is on: its row says Current in words, is marked aria-current (page when it is a link, true when it is a button) and, when you leave expanded to the list, its module starts open. state is completed, locked, preview or available (the default, which says nothing): a locked lesson is not a link or a button, takes no tab stop and says why through reason; a preview lesson is marked Preview. A lesson with an href is a link and onSelect(lesson, module, event) runs on it, so a client-side router can call event.preventDefault(); without an href but with onSelect it is a button. expanded (the ids of the open modules) with onExpandedChange controls the folds; defaultExpanded only sets where they start. Several modules can be open at once. The open and close animation is height-based and switches off under reduced motion. labels carries every word, with {done}, {total} and {count} filled in.

items.name: class-session-card
items.title: Class session card
items.description: A class you can book: date tile, time and length, coach, room and level, spots left with a fill bar, and a Book, Join waitlist or Cancel action.
items.docs: start and end are exact moments (a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string with its offset); timeZone is where the session takes place and every time on the card is written in it, locale is the language, and the length is worked out from the two. spots is how many places are left and capacity how many there are in all: together they write '3 spots left of 14' and fill a real progress bar named 'Spots taken' that is read as '11 of 14 spots taken'. An open session with no spots left turns into a full one, which says 'All 14 spots taken' in words of its own ('Class full' when it does not know its capacity). status is open, full, booked or cancelled: open shows Book (onBook), full shows Join waitlist (onWaitlist, falling back to onBook), booked shows a 'Booked' badge with a check and Cancel (onCancel), and cancelled mutes the card, strikes the title and the time through and drops the actions. Every handler may return a promise: the button keeps its focus and shows a spinner with aria-busy while it runs, a rejection shows an alert saying that nothing was changed (press the button again to retry), and each result is announced politely in a status region. The buttons are named with the class and its time, so a list of them is not a list of 'Book'. coach is a name or { name, image? } (initials stand in for a missing picture), room and level are plain words, headingLevel sets the title's level, and labels carries every word for translation.

items.name: service-card
items.title: Service card
items.description: A bookable service: name, what is included, and duration and price as a labelled pair, with a select or book action and a from-price state.
items.docs: duration is a number of minutes (written '45 min', '1 h 30 min') or your own words ('Half a day'); price is a number written in the currency and locale you name, with whole amounts losing their cents and 0 saying 'Free', or your own words ('On request'). Duration and price are a description list, so a screen reader hears 'Duration: 45 min' and 'Price: from €60, 3 options'. priceFrom, or options of two or more, writes 'from' before the price and counts the options after it. includes is a short check list and badge puts a word beside the name. Giving onSelect or selected makes the action a toggle with aria-pressed, controlled with selected or uncontrolled with defaultSelected: picked, it shows a check, a heavier border and 'Selected', and the whole card is a place to click. The action is named with the words on it and then the service ('Select Colour and tone', 'Selected Colour and tone'), so a voice control that says what it sees reaches it. With href and no onSelect the action is a link, 'Book'; with both, the name links to href. unavailable is the reason a service cannot be booked: it is written on the card, the card mutes, and the action is aria-disabled and described by the reason, so keyboard users still find it and hear why. labels carries every word.

items.name: specialist-card
items.title: Specialist card
items.description: A person you can book: photo, name, specialties, languages, rating and the next free slot in words, with a book action kept apart from the profile link.
items.docs: name is the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router; without an href but with onOpen it becomes a button) and the Book button (onBook) is its own target above it, named with the person. image falls back to initials, taken from the name without the titles in front of it ('Dr. Ines Kowalski' is IK) or from initials when you give them. rating and ratingCount draw the stars to the exact average and are read as a sentence ('Rated 4.9 out of 5 from 128 reviews'); a count of zero says 'No reviews yet'. specialties and languages are word chips under their own labels. nextAvailable is an exact moment, written the way a person says it ('Today, 16:45', 'Tomorrow, 10:30', 'Thursday, 14:15', then '12 Nov, 09:00') in a time element, counted in timeZone against now: leave now out to use the browser's clock after the first paint, and until then the slot is written as a date so the server and the browser agree. null says 'No slots this week' and disables Book (aria-disabled, described by that line); leave it out to show no slot at all. labels carries every word.

items.name: vehicle-card
items.title: Vehicle card
items.description: A vehicle listing for a dealer: photo gallery, price with an optional monthly figure, key specs as a labelled list, status in words and a save button.
items.docs: images is { src, alt }[] and every photo needs its alt: the gallery is a carousel group whose slides read 'Photo 2 of 6', steps with the arrows (which wrap around) or a swipe, and a click or a tap on a photo opens the listing. One photo has no arrows; none shows a quiet placeholder, and so does a photo that does not load. Photos load lazily; priority fetches the first one at once, for the card above the fold. title is make and model and the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router), variant the trim under it. price is a number written whole in the currency and locale you name, large and in tabular numerals, or your own words; monthlyPrice adds 'or €459 / month'. year, mileage (with mileageUnit, km or mi, written with its unit by Intl), fuel, transmission and power are a description list, and a last spec on its own takes the full row. status is available, reserved or sold: reserved gets a dashed badge with a clock glyph and sold a solid one, both with the word on the first photo, both mute the title, the price and the specs, and a sold vehicle's photos lose their colour. saved, defaultSaved and onSave make a heart toggle with aria-pressed, named 'Save Halcyon E-Tourer', above the card's link; leave them out for no heart. labels carries every word.

items.name: venue-card
items.title: Venue card
items.description: A local business in a directory: photo, name, category, rating, price level, distance and an open-now status in words, with a save button.
items.docs: name is the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router). image is an address or { src, alt }; without one a quiet tile says 'No photo yet', and a photo that does not load gets the same tile saying 'Photo unavailable'. category, priceLevel and distance sit on one line: priceLevel is 1 to 4, drawn as priceSymbol repeated with the unspent symbols faint and said to screen readers as Inexpensive, Moderate, Expensive or Very expensive, and distance is a number of metres (written '450 m', '1.2 km', or with units='imperial' '0.3 mi' and '350 ft') or your own words. rating and ratingCount draw the stars to the exact average and read as a sentence. openNow says whether the venue is open, as a word with a glyph: a filled dot and 'Open until 22:00', a hollow one and 'Closed, opens at 09:30'. You work it out from the venue's own clock; the card only says it. closesAt and opensAt are a wall-clock string ('22:00', written as it says in the locale) or a moment written in timeZone. tags show the first three as chips and count the rest. saved, defaultSaved and onSave make a heart toggle with aria-pressed, named 'Save Café Halcyon', above the card's link. labels carries every word.

items.name: tour-card
items.title: Tour card
items.description: A guided tour or activity in a listing: photo, title, duration, group size, languages, rating and the price from, with cancellation stated in words.
items.docs: title is the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router). image is an address or { src, alt } (a photo that does not load gives way to a quiet tile) and badge a word on it; location sits above the title. duration is a number of minutes, written in words by Intl in the reader's language ('1 hour 30 minutes', '3 uur'), or your own words; groupSize is a number ('Up to 12 people') or words; languages is a short list ('English, Dutch'). The facts are a description list, so each is read with its name. cancellation is true for 'Free cancellation', a string for your own words, and the line is left out when it is not offered. priceFrom is the lowest price per person in whole units of the currency, written 'From €45 per person' by Intl. rating and ratingCount draw the stars to the exact average and read as a sentence. soldOut is true or a reason: the hint at the foot says 'Sold out' in place of 'Check availability', the price is muted, and a string says why on the card; the title stays a link so people can still find other dates. saved, defaultSaved and onSave make a heart toggle with aria-pressed above the card's link. labels carries every word, locale the numbers, the units and the currency.

items.name: app-listing-card
items.title: App listing card
items.description: An app in a directory or store: icon, name, developer, rating and size, with an action that goes from Get to a progress, then Open or Update.
items.docs: name is the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router). icon is an address; the initials of the name stand in while it loads or if it fails. state is get, installing, installed or update and the action follows it: Get, Installing with its percentage and a progress bar along its foot (progress is 0 to 100; leave it out for a bar of unknown length), Open or Update, each named with the app ('Get Pocketwise'). It is one button throughout, busy and inert while the app installs, so keyboard focus stays on it from Get to Open. Beside the text it shows just the percentage, as wide as Get was, so the text does not move when the install starts; under the text it says 'Installing 42%'. onAction receives the state it was pressed in. A change of state is announced politely once ('Installing Pocketwise', 'Pocketwise installed. You can open it now.'), never every percent. rating and ratingCount draw the stars to the exact average and read as a sentence ('Rated 4.7 from 12,400 ratings'). size is a number of bytes, written '48 MB', or your own words; version '3.2.1' is written 'v3.2.1'. On a card narrower than 24rem the action moves under the text. labels carries every word.

items.name: fundraiser-card
items.title: Fundraiser card
items.description: A fundraiser: the story in a line, the amount raised against the goal as a real progress bar, donors, days left, the organiser and a donate action.
items.docs: raised and goal are whole units of the currency: the card writes '€4,820 raised of €10,000' with the percentage beside it (rounded down, and never 100% before the goal is reached), and a progress bar named 'Fundraising progress' that is read in the same words, so the figure is in text and the bar only repeats it. At or over the goal it says 'Goal reached' in place of the percentage and keeps the donate button. donors and the days left are a description list; days are counted in timeZone between now and endsAt ('Days left 12', 'Ends Today'), and leaving now out reads the browser's clock after the first paint (until then the end date is written). Once endsAt has passed the card says 'Ended on 3 Oct', hides the donate button and mutes the picture. organiser is { name, image? }, credited with an avatar. A picture that does not load gives way to a quiet tile of the same shape. With href (or onOpen) the title is the one link of the card, and the Donate button (onDonate) stays its own target above it. labels carries every word.

items.name: delivery-stop-card
items.title: Delivery stop card
items.description: One stop on a delivery route: sequence marker, recipient and address, time window and parcels, with call, navigate and outcome actions.
items.docs: sequence is the stop's number, written in a marker; address is { recipient, lines, notes? }; window is { from, to }, written in locale and timeZone ('12:30 – 13:00') and read as 'Delivery window'; parcels counts the parcels. status is upcoming, next, delivered, failed or skipped. The next stop is emphasised, carries a 'Next stop' badge and aria-current='step', and gets large Call (onCall), Navigate (onNavigate) and Delivered buttons, with Could not deliver and Skip one tap away in a menu; every outcome is reported through onStatusChange('delivered' | 'failed' | 'skipped'). An upcoming stop shows Call and Navigate. A stop that is done mutes and says what happened in its badge, in words and with the time ('Delivered at 11:52', from completedAt), shows reason in a callout (an error one when it failed), and offers Undo, which reports 'upcoming' so that you decide which stop is next. The card is one stop and keeps no order of its own: put them in a list, and in a sortable list for route planning. Every change of status is said once in a polite status line ('Stop 3, Sana Haddad: Delivered at 11:52'), and when the control that had focus leaves the card, focus stays inside it: on Undo after an outcome, on the first action after Undo, on the card itself when it has none. Focus you have moved on yourself, to the next stop, is left where you put it. labels carries every word.

items.name: book-card
items.title: Book card
items.description: A book in a catalogue: a 2:3 cover with a typographic fallback, title, authors, rating, formats and whether it is available, reserved or out on loan.
items.docs: title is the one link of the card (href); authors are written as a list in the reader's language ('Tom Calder and Ana Ruiz'). cover is an address or { src, alt }, kept in a 2:3 box from the first paint; a typographic tile with the title and the first author sits under it, so it also stands in while the picture loads, when there is none and when it fails. rating and ratingCount draw the stars to the exact average and read as a sentence. formats (print, ebook, audio) are word chips. availability is available, reserved or out, written in words with a glyph; for out, dueDate ('2026-11-12' is the day it says in any time zone, any other moment is written in timeZone) adds 'Due back 12 Nov'. price is a number in the currency and locale you name, whole amounts losing their cents, or your own words ('Free to borrow'). orientation is horizontal (the cover beside the text, for lists) or vertical (the cover on a quiet shelf above it, for grids). The card keeps no state and renders on the server; only the cover is a small client component, which takes itself away when the picture fails to load, so the jacket shows. labels carries every word.

items.name: recipe-card
items.title: Recipe card
items.description: A recipe in a card: photo, title, total time with prep and cook in a tooltip, difficulty, servings, dietary marks as words and a rating.
items.docs: time is minutes in all (45) or { prep, cook, total? } in minutes: it is written in the locale's short units ('45 min', '1 hr 15 min'), and when both prep and cook are given the breakdown opens in a tooltip on hover, on focus and on a tap (a press of the button toggles it, so a touch screen and a screen reader reach it too, and a tap outside closes it; the total is prep plus cook unless you give it). difficulty is easy, medium or hard, written as a word beside three small bars; servings reads 'Serves 4'. dietary is a list of words and every one is shown, so nobody has to open the recipe to learn that it holds nuts or dairy: never icons alone. rating (0 to 5) and ratingCount draw the stars and are read as one sentence ('Rated 4.6 from 212 reviews'); a count of 0 says 'No reviews yet'. title is the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router; without an href but with onOpen it becomes a button), and image falls back to a quiet 'No photo yet' tile, also when the picture fails to load. The heart beside the title is a toggle with aria-pressed, named with the recipe ('Save Lemon ricotta pasta as a favourite'): controlled with saved and onSave, or uncontrolled with defaultSaved. Without saved or onSave it keeps its own state, so a prototype works at once; saveable={false} removes it. It is its own target above the card's link. labels carries every word.

items.description: A working preview of Recipe card.

items.name: ingredient-list
items.title: Ingredient list
items.description: A recipe's ingredients that scale: change the servings and the amounts follow, as kitchen fractions or metric decimals, with lines you can tick off.
items.docs: ingredients are lines with an id, name, quantity, unit, note and group, written for baseServings. A numeric quantity scales with the servings; a string quantity ('a pinch', 'a handful') stays as written, and scales: false keeps a number fixed. A line with no quantity is a name with a note ('maple syrup, to taste'). Cups, spoons, ounces and pounds are written as kitchen fractions ('1 1/2 cups') and never as decimals: an amount snaps to the nearest eighth or third (a tie goes up, and 1/8 is the least), counted things come in quarters, and a name with a plural takes it ('1 egg', '3 eggs'); grams and millilitres are decimals that roll over to kilograms and litres at a thousand. Units pluralise through Intl.PluralRules by the amount as it is written ('1 cup', '2 cups', and '3/4 cup' stays singular), the metric and imperial ones take the locale's own short form, and units lets you add words or translate them. servings is controlled with onServingsChange or uncontrolled with defaultServings; the stepper is the kit's number input, and Reset appears after a change. checkable adds a checkbox to each line: a ticked line is struck through and stays where it is, the count ('2 of 9 ticked') is a polite live region, and Clear ticks empties them; checked, defaultChecked and onCheckedChange control which. Lines with the same group sit under one heading, and the amounts line up in one column across groups. labels carries every word.

items.title: Ingredient list demo
items.description: A working preview of Ingredient list.

items.name: match-score-card
items.title: Match score card
items.description: A fixture or result: two teams, the score, the state (live, full time or kickoff time) and the competition, read as one sentence.
items.docs: home and away are { name, logo?, score? } and status is scheduled, live or finished. A live match shows 'Live' beside a pulsing dot that holds still under reduced motion, with the minute written 'N min' (a number, or text such as '45+2'); a finished one shows 'Full time' and, when kickoff is given, its date; a scheduled one shows the kickoff time and date, or 'TBC' without one. kickoff is an exact moment (a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string with its offset) written in timeZone and locale, so the server and the browser agree. Scores are tabular, and the winner of a finished match is set in heavier type and said in words ('Halcyon FC won', or 'Draw'). The card is read as one sentence and its drawing is hidden from assistive technology: 'Halcyon FC 2, Kestrel United 1, full time', 'Halcyon FC 2, Kestrel United 1, live, 67 minutes' or 'Halcyon FC versus Kestrel United, Sunday 9 November, 14:30'. With href the whole card is the link. A missing crest becomes the team's initials, and long names are cut with an ellipsis and carry the full name as their title. The score column grows for a score of three digits, and the scores keep one right edge. labels carries every word.

items.name: player-card
items.title: Player card
items.description: A squad member for a club site: portrait, shirt number, name, position, nationality and season stats, with injured and suspended players marked in words.
items.docs: name is the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router; without an href but with onOpen it becomes a button). number is set large beside the name and read as 'Number 9'; position is always a word, with an optional positionCode ('FW') drawn as a small tag that is not read. stats are label and value pairs (three or four fit) in a description list with tabular numerals, kept at the foot so a grid of cards lines up whatever each one has, and every card has the same 4:5 portrait. The figures sit in columns once the card is 12.5rem wide (16rem for four) and as rows of label and figure below that, in capitals only from 17rem, and a label that is too long is cut with an ellipsis and never runs into the next figure. A missing photo, or one that fails to load, becomes a tonal tile with the initials. status is fit, injured or suspended: the last two are marked in words in a bar across the photo, 'Injured' or 'Suspended', with returns written as you want it read ('Back around 24 Nov'), and the photo loses some of its colour. In a card narrower than 8.5rem the bar keeps to the word, and the return is still read aloud. captain puts a 'Captain' badge on the photo. nationality and age (read as '24 years') sit under the position. The card answers to its own width, not the screen's: in a column narrower than 12rem the number sits above the name instead of beside it, so a two-column squad grid on a phone still reads. labels carries every word.

items.name: availability-calendar
items.title: Availability calendar
items.description: A read-only calendar of free, booked and on-request days for rentals, venues and rooms, told apart by pattern and a legend in words, never by colour.
items.docs: booked and onRequest are lists of days ('2026-03-14') and runs ({ start, end }, both included): a day is a day on the calendar, so nothing shifts with a time zone, and a booked day wins over a day on request. Every day is a grid cell named in full ('Friday 14 March, available', '..., booked', '..., on request', '..., past'), with a pattern of its own: blank for free, a diagonal hatch for booked, dots and a dashed edge for on request. The legend names them in words, and minStay writes 'Minimum stay: 3 nights' beside it. On a hatched or dotted day the number sits on a small chip, so the pattern never runs through it. The grid is a keyboard grid with one tab stop: arrow keys move by day and week, Home and End to the ends of the week, Page Up and Page Down by month (Shift for a year), and the view follows. months is 1 or 2: two months sit side by side, each with its own title and an arrow at the outer edge, once the calendar itself is 36rem wide (a container query), and stack with one toolbar above them when it is narrower. today ('2026-03-09') mutes the days before it and puts a dot under it; leave it out to use the browser's clock in timeZone, read once the page is live: until then, and unless defaultMonth or month names the month, the calendar only holds its place at a fixed height and the grid appears once the page is live, so a page that is built ahead of time (static, cached) should pass defaultMonth. month and onMonthChange control the first month shown, or defaultMonth sets it. locale writes the month and day names, weekStartsOn is 1 (Monday) or 0, and labels carries every word. It only displays: pair it with the date range picker when people must choose dates.

items.title: Availability calendar demo
items.description: A working preview of Availability calendar.

items.name: membership-card
items.title: Membership card
items.description: A digital membership card: member, tier, member since and valid until, with a QR code that opens large for scanning and a copyable member number.
items.docs: member is { name, number, image? } and tier is set large. since is written as month and year and validUntil as a date, in locale and timeZone (a day such as '2027-01-17' never shifts with the zone). qr is a node, so you can pass the kit's QR code, an svg, an img or your own: it must fill its box and be drawn with dark modules, because the code always sits on a white tile, in light and in dark. Tapping the tile opens the same code large in a dialog, also on white, with the name and number below it, for scanning. The member number is a mono value with a copy button that says when it is copied. status is active or expired: an expired card says 'Expired on 3 Mar 2026', mutes the tier and the picture, and hides the code, so nobody holds up something that no longer opens the door. organisation replaces the small line at the top, and it wraps to two lines before it is cut. The card answers to its own width: on a narrow card the code sits beside the tier and the member takes a full row below. The card is named by the member and the tier ('Maya Okafor, Gold membership'), and labels carries every word.

items.title: Membership card demo

items.name: certificate-card
items.title: Certificate card
items.description: A certificate of completion as a card: recipient, course, dates, a copyable credential ID, and download and verify actions that still read in black and white.
items.docs: recipient and title are set large inside a double frame, with issuer, issuedAt and expiresAt in a labelled list in locale and timeZone (a day such as '2026-01-12' never shifts with the zone). credentialId is a mono value you can copy. verifyHref is a link that opens in a new tab (rel noopener) and says so to screen readers; onDownload may return a promise, and the button then shows a spinner until it settles. A certificate whose expiresAt has passed, or one you mark with expired, says 'Expired on 3 Mar 2026' in a badge and mutes its frame and seal (the list then leaves the end date out, because the badge has it); left to the clock it reads as valid until the page is live, so the server and the browser agree. The card is an article whose heading is the title (headingLevel sets its level), and when it is printed the buttons give way to the address that verifies it and every border and text falls back to black on white, on a dark page as well. labels carries every word.

items.title: Certificate card demo
items.description: A working preview of Certificate card.

items.name: stamp-card
items.title: Stamp card
items.description: A digital loyalty stamp card: a grid of stamps with the filled ones drawn, the reward on the last one, and a Redeem button once the card is full.
items.docs: total is how many stamps the card has and filled how many are given; they sit in a grid (ten make two rows of five) of circles, the filled ones in the foreground with a check, the empty ones dashed and counting up, and the last one is the reward, drawn with a gift. The card reads as one sentence ('Cappuccino card, 6 of 10 stamps, 4 to go') and the grid is hidden from assistive technology. When filled goes up, each new stamp plays a short press (skipped under reduced motion) and the new count is announced politely. A full card changes its badge to 'Reward ready' and, with onRedeem, shows a Redeem button named with the reward; onRedeem may return a promise and the button shows a spinner until it settles. Without it a full card only says that the reward is unlocked. lastStampedAt is written as a short date in locale and timeZone. label is the heading, headingLevel sets its level, and labels carries every word.

items.title: Stamp card demo
items.description: A working preview of Stamp card.

items.name: match-timeline
items.title: Match timeline
items.description: The events of a match on a centre line: goals, cards and substitutions with the minute, the player and the side, in one column on a phone.
items.docs: events are { id, minute, extraMinute?, side, type, player, assist?, detail? } in any order: they are sorted by the clock, and added time reads '45+2'. type is goal, penalty, own-goal, penalty-missed, yellow-card, red-card or substitution, and each has an icon and a word, so it reads without colour (a yellow card is an outlined card, a red one a solid card). The running score is written after every goal, penalty and own goal (an own goal counts for the other side). Home events sit on the left of the line and away events on the right once the timeline itself is 32rem wide (a container query, so it works in a sidebar as well as a page), under the two team names; below that everything runs in one column and each event names its team. status is finished (the default: a labelled 'Half time' break at halfTimeAt, 45 by default, and 'Full time' with the score), live (ending in a pulsing 'Live' that holds still under reduced motion) or scheduled. Goals have a solid icon, the rest a quiet one. It is an ordered list, and each line is read as one sentence in the order minute, event, player, team, score whatever side it sits on ('Minute 45 plus 2, Penalty, Mila Kowalski, Halcyon FC, Score 2 to 1'). For a substitution player is who comes on and detail names who goes off. labels carries every word.

items.title: Match timeline demo
items.description: A working preview of Match timeline.

items.name: season-strip
items.title: Season strip
items.description: Twelve months in a strip that show when something is at its best, with states you read without colour, a legend in words and a note in a tooltip.
items.docs: months is twelve entries from January to December, each 'best', 'good', 'off' or 'closed', or { state, note } with a note that opens in a tooltip on hover, focus or tap. Each month is a tile with its short name and a state drawn as a fill: solid and bold for the best months, a lighter fill for the good ones, an empty outline out of season and a hatch when closed, with a legend in words, so colour never carries the meaning. A screen reader first hears one sentence ('Best in April, May and September'), then each month with its state. The current month is ringed and marked 'Now' in words once the browser's clock is read, or from now when you pin it. firstMonth (1 to 12) starts the strip somewhere else without reordering the data, locale writes the month names and the sentence, timeZone decides which month it is, and labels carries every word. Twelve tiles in a row where there is room, two rows of six on a phone.

items.title: Season strip demo
items.description: A working preview of Season strip.

items.name: color-token-card
items.title: Color token card
items.description: A design colour documented: swatch, name and token, a value that copies as hex, rgb or oklch, and its contrast on white and black with pass marks.
items.docs: name, value, token and usage describe the colour. value may be hex ('#0A7D5C'), rgb ('rgb(10 125 92)') or oklch ('oklch(0.55 0.115 169)'), with or without alpha, and is read in the browser. The card starts on the format the value is written in, and keeps its digits when that format is showing; one button cycles through copyFormats (hex, rgb, oklch by default) and the other copies what is showing, with the result said politely (onCopied is called with the text and its format). Contrast against white and black is worked out with the WCAG 2 formula on the 8-bit values (a colour with alpha is laid over each background first), and each result is a grade in words with a glyph: AAA with a double check, AA with a check, 'AA large' with a warning for large text only, Fail with a cross. A screen reader hears one sentence per result ('4.8:1 on white, AA: meets AA for text of any size'). A value that is not hex, rgb or oklch is shown as written and gets no contrast. Put the cards in a grid for a palette page. labels carries every word and locale writes the numbers.

items.name: color-token-card-demo
items.title: Color token card demo
items.description: A working preview of Color token card.

items.name: team-clocks
items.title: Team clocks
items.description: The time for each teammate: name, city and local time as a list or an analog face, with Working or Off hours in words and the offset to you.
items.docs: people lists the team with a name, a time zone and optionally a city, an image and workHours (start, end and days; the default is 09:00 to 17:00 on weekdays, and an end before the start is a shift through midnight). Each entry shows the local time, the weekday in front of it when it differs from the reader's day ('Tue 08:30'), the offset to the reader after the city ('+6 h', said in full to a screen reader; a long city wraps and the offset is never cut) and 'Working' with a sun or 'Off hours' with a moon, as words. variant is 'list' (one row per person, with their picture or initials) or 'analog' (a card with an SVG face and the digital time beside it as text, in as many columns as the box it sits in has room for, not as many as the screen has: one to a row in a narrow box, then two, then three). hour12 writes 8:30 AM instead of 08:30, and sort='offset' puts the team in order of UTC offset. The clocks tick once a minute, on the minute, and again when a sleeping tab wakes. They wait for the browser's clock before drawing a time, so the server and the browser never disagree, or take now to pin the moment. The reader's zone is read in the browser, or passed as viewerTimeZone.

items.name: achievement-tile
items.title: Achievement tile
items.description: A badge you earned or can still earn: icon, name, how to get it, and a locked, in progress or unlocked state that reads in words, with a one-time shine.
items.docs: title and description are the heading and the how-to-earn line, which stays visible in every state. state is 'locked' (an outline, dim, with the word Locked), 'progress' (a bar with '7 of 10' in text, from progress { current, goal }) or 'unlocked' (a filled tile with the date from unlockedAt, written in locale and timeZone; a date-only string is a day on the calendar). Every tile has the same minimum height and fills its grid cell, so a row lines up. When the state changes to unlocked after the tile was drawn, a short shine crosses it once (left out under reduced motion) and the unlock is announced politely. icon is any node, drawn at 20px. labels carries every word.

items.name: achievement-tile-demo
items.title: Achievement tile demo
items.description: A working preview of Achievement tile.

items.name: stack-trace
items.title: Stack trace
items.description: An error's stack trace made readable: your own frames in full weight, library frames folded away, copyable file locations and one button for the whole trace.
items.docs: Pass an error ({ name, message, stack }) and the stack is parsed into frames (V8's 'at fn (file:1:2)' and the 'fn@file:1:2' of Firefox and Safari), or pass frames you parsed yourself. Frames in node_modules, in Node's own modules, in native code or outside projectRoot are library code: runs of them fold under 'Show 8 library frames' with the packages they come from, or are open from the start with defaultExpanded. Your own frames show the function in full weight with the file location under it, relative to projectRoot, and the first one is set apart as 'Start here'. Every file location is a button that copies 'src/cart.tsx:42:13' (its copy glyph shows on hover and focus, and always on a touch screen, and a long path wraps after a slash and not in the middle of a file name), and Copy trace copies the whole trace as plain text, the original stack when you gave one. The frames are an ordered list under a heading, and copies are announced politely (onCopied is called with the text); a clipboard that refuses is said on the card too, in words, not only to a screen reader. parseStack and the other helpers are in stack-trace/parse for servers and tests.

items.title: Stack trace demo
items.description: A working preview of Stack trace.

items.name: offline-state
items.title: Offline state
items.description: The page-sized 'you are offline' state: what still works on the device, a Try again button, and a Back online moment with an automatic retry.
items.docs: It follows the browser's online and offline events, or your own online prop, and it is hidden whenever the browser knows it is online, including the first paint. Offline it shows a wifi-off icon, 'You are offline', what is safe on the device, an optional last-saved line from cachedAt (written in locale and timeZone), your children under 'Still works offline', and a Try again button that calls onRetry, shows a spinner and says 'Still offline' if it did not help, on a line that has its room from the start so the button never moves. When the connection returns it says 'Back online' for a moment, calls onRetry once and steps aside. The change is announced through a polite status region and focus never moves. It is page-sized: cover your page with className='fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-background' or place it in the content area. The title is a heading at headingLevel (2 by default, 1 when the state is the whole page). labels carries every word.

items.name: offline-state-demo
items.title: Offline state demo
items.description: A working preview of Offline state.

items.name: first-run-state
items.title: First run state
items.description: The empty state for a brand new account: one promise and two to four ways to begin, as cards in one keyboard group, with a Recommended one and a quiet Skip.
items.docs: title is the one promise and description a line of context. options are two to four ways to begin ({ id, title, description, icon, onSelect or href }): a card with href is a link, any other is a button. recommendedId puts the word Recommended on one card, and onSkip adds a quiet 'Skip for now'. The cards are one labelled group: Tab reaches each card, and the arrow keys, Home and End move between them, up and down to the nearest card in the row above or below. Two and four cards sit in two columns, three in a row once the container is wide enough, and all stack on a phone. It is deliberately not a checklist: nothing is ticked and nothing counts. Use Empty State when there is nothing to choose.
