items.title: First run state demo
items.description: A working preview of First run state.

items.name: unavailable-state
items.title: Unavailable state
items.description: For a link that no longer works (expired, used, revoked or removed): the reason in words, the date it happened and the next step, with a resend cooldown.
items.docs: reason is 'expired', 'used', 'revoked' or 'removed': each has its own icon, title and explanation, and subject names what the link was ('invite', 'reset link'). occurredAt is written as a date in locale and timeZone (a date-only string as a day). The action fits the reason: expired offers onRequestNew, used offers signInHref first, revoked and removed offer homeHref. Asking for a new link shows a spinner while onRequestNew runs, then a cooldown (cooldownSeconds, default 30) with the seconds left, and says politely when the request went through, when it failed and when asking is possible again, on a line that has its room from the start so the card does not grow. It never shows a technical code. children add a line under the actions. The title is a heading at headingLevel (2 by default, 1 when the state is the whole page). labels carries every word.

items.name: unavailable-state-demo
items.title: Unavailable state demo
items.description: A working preview of Unavailable state.

items.name: update-available-bar
items.title: Update available bar
items.description: A slim bar saying a new version is ready, with Reload now, Later (remembered for the session) and a link to what changed. Announced once, never steals focus.
items.docs: onReload reloads into the new version: wire it to your service worker's skipWaiting message and reload on controllerchange, or to location.reload(), which is also what the button does without it. Reload shows a busy state while the page restarts. onLater is called after the bar was hidden; Later also remembers the snooze for snoozeMinutes (60 by default) in sessionStorage, per version, so the bar comes back after the interval and not on every navigation. version, appName and changesHref add the version, the product's name and a 'What changed' link. position is 'top' (the default: in the flow of the page, above everything, so it pushes the page down instead of covering the header, and scrolls away with the page) or 'bottom' (fixed over the bottom edge of the viewport, clearing the safe-area inset; className='absolute' places it inside a box of your own). sticky keeps a top bar in view while the page scrolls, and writes its height as it grows in and out to --update-bar-height on the element it sits in, so a sticky header can hang under it with top-[var(--update-bar-height,0px)] instead of being covered; put the bar in the element that holds the page, because it sticks inside its parent. It grows or slides in and out (it appears at once under reduced motion), is announced once through a status region and never takes focus.

items.title: Update available bar demo
items.description: A working preview of Update available bar.

items.name: mode-bar
items.title: Mode bar
items.description: A bar that says you are in a special mode (test data, viewing as someone else, read-only or beta) and gives the one way out. It cannot be dismissed.
items.docs: kind is 'test', 'viewing-as', 'read-only' or 'beta': each has its own icon, its own word in a chip and its own weight (hatched, inverted, plain, a card), so the mode reads without colour. title adds whose account it is for viewing-as, description says what is different in plain words, and onExit adds the single Exit button, named 'Exit: Test mode' for a screen reader. There is no close button on purpose: a mode that can be hidden is how mistakes on real data happen. Without onExit there is no button at all, for a mode the person cannot leave. The bar is a labelled region, so screen reader users can jump to it. sticky pins it under the header; pass className='top-14' to sit under a 56px header. labels carries every word.

items.title: Mode bar demo
items.description: A working preview of Mode bar.

items.name: trial-status-bar
items.title: Trial status bar
items.description: A header strip counting the days left in a trial, with a thin progress line and an Upgrade button that gets firmer in the last days and after the end.
items.docs: startedAt and endsAt are ISO moments, timeZone is the zone days are counted in, and now pins the clock for tests. With four days or more left it reads 'Trial: 12 days left' with the date it ends and an outline Upgrade; from three days on the sentence changes ('Trial ends in 3 days', 'Trial ends tomorrow', 'Trial ends today'), the bar turns solid and Upgrade stands out; after the end it reads 'Your trial has ended' with the same action. Days are calendar days in timeZone, so the number only changes at midnight there. The thin track shows how much of the trial has passed and is hidden from assistive technology. The strip keeps its height until the browser's clock is read, so the page does not jump. onUpgrade is called on press, or give upgradeHref for a link.

items.name: payment-failed-banner
items.title: Payment failed banner
items.description: A banner for a failed subscription payment: which card, the date it becomes a problem, and one button to fix it. Turns destructive once access is paused.
items.docs: cardLabel is what follows "your" ("card ending 4242"), graceEndsAt is the end of the grace period and status is 'grace' (the default) or 'overdue', which turns the banner destructive and says that access is paused. onUpdate runs when Update payment method is pressed and may return a promise: the button shows a spinner until it settles and then takes the focus back, which a disabled button loses. invoiceHref adds a quiet View invoice link. The date is a time element written in timeZone and locale, with the full day, time and zone in its title. There is no close button on purpose: render the banner only while the payment is unresolved. The banner is a labelled region, not a live one. labels carries every word.

items.description: A working preview of Payment failed banner.

items.name: verify-email-banner
items.title: Verify email banner
items.description: A banner for unverified accounts that names the address, resends the email with a cooldown that survives a reload, and lets people fix a typo.
items.docs: email is the address to verify and reason finishes the sentence ("to start sending invites"). onResend returns a promise: a rejection shows its message under the buttons and does not start the wait. After a send the button counts down for cooldownSeconds (60), worked out from timestamps and kept in sessionStorage under storageKey, so a reload does not reset it; the countdown is spoken at its start and its end only, while the button's own name is what it shows ("Resend in 28s"), so voice control can reach it. onChangeEmail(address) turns the address into a field: return an error message to show under it, or nothing, and the new address gets its own email and its own wait. When verified turns true the banner swaps to a short Email verified and folds away; if it is true on first render nothing is drawn. labels carries every word.

items.description: A working preview of Verify email banner.

items.name: bulk-result-summary
items.title: Bulk result summary
items.description: The outcome of a batch job in numbers: what worked, what was skipped and what failed, with each failure's reason and a retry.
items.docs: total, succeeded, skipped and failures ({ id, label, reason }[]) give the counts; a fourth, not processed, appears when they do not add up to total. verb ("Imported") and noun ("contacts", or { one, other }) write the headline. With no failures the panel is one calm line. More than foldAfter (5) failures fold behind Show all n. onRetryFailed and onDownloadReport may return promises and show a spinner meanwhile; when Retry settles the panel takes the focus, so a screen reader reads the new counts (settle it once they are in), and Download report takes its own focus back. The bar never relies on colour: each part has a pattern (solid, dots, hatch) and a written count, and a screen reader hears the counts as the panel's description. The panel takes focus once on mount unless autoFocus is false.

items.title: Bulk result summary demo
items.description: A working preview of Bulk result summary.

items.name: batch-progress
items.title: Batch progress
items.description: Progress for work on many items at once: one bar, a count of done, failed and waiting, and a Cancel that stops the rest.
items.docs: total, done and failed are counts of items; done and failed are kept apart, so the bar shows done plus failed and the rest is waiting. label names the progress bar. status is 'running', 'cancelling' or 'complete'; onCancel adds the Cancel button, and on complete it gives way to Done. The failed share is hatched at the end of the bar, never thinner than 6px, so a few failures in a big batch still show. The bar is a real progressbar with aria-valuetext; the counts line is not a live region, and a status is spoken only at each tenth of the way, when cancelling starts and when the batch is done.

items.title: Batch progress demo

items.name: permission-primer
items.title: Permission primer
items.description: The soft ask before the browser's permission prompt: why you need notifications, camera, microphone or location, and what to do if blocked.
items.docs: kind picks the permission (notifications, camera, microphone or location), with its icon and words; benefit is one line on what the person gets. onRequest asks the browser and returns its answer; leave it out and the card asks the browser itself. state fixes the permission for a preview, or when you track it yourself; otherwise the card reads the browser (the Permissions API, or Notification.permission) and follows changes made in its settings. Not now is remembered in localStorage for snoozeDays (14) under storageKey. The browser's own prompt opens only from the Allow button, never on load, and the card is drawn after the page is live. If the browser closes its prompt without an answer, or cannot ask, the card says so (spoken too) and Allow takes the focus back. labels carries every word, including the steps shown when it is blocked.

items.name: pwa-install-prompt
items.title: PWA install prompt
items.description: A prompt to install your web app: a real Install button where the browser supports it, and share-sheet steps on iPhone.
items.docs: It listens for beforeinstallprompt and shows Install with Not now; on iOS Safari, which has no such event, it shows the Share, then Add to Home Screen steps after delay ms. It is hidden when the app already runs standalone, a dismissal is remembered in localStorage for dismissDays (14), and it never appears on first paint. platform="ios" forces the steps for a preview. The root is a window-sized, click-through box that the card measures itself against: a bottom sheet below 36rem and a corner card above, with safe-area padding; pass className="absolute" to place it inside a box of your own. Mount it once, high in the app, so it is listening before the browser fires its event. icon is an element for the app tile; onInstalled and onDismiss are callbacks.

items.title: PWA install prompt demo
items.description: A working preview of PWA install prompt.

items.name: queue-position
items.title: Queue position
items.description: A waiting-room panel for being in line: your place, an honest wait range, and a Leave button that asks before it lets go of the spot.
items.docs: position is the place (1 is next); total, joinedAt (written in timeZone), startPosition (the bar fills from there; default the farthest back the panel has seen) and estimateSeconds (written as a range, never a promise) fill in the rest. status 'ready' shows It is your turn with the action (onEnter) and the hold counting down (holdSeconds, or holdEndsAt from your server), then calls onExpire when it runs out. onLeave runs on the second press of Leave the line. The number counts through whole places to each new place, and its suffix steps aside while it counts when a place on the way would need another one (5th to 2nd); Enter now takes the focus back once its promise settles. A screen reader is told the place only every fifth place and for each of the last three, and the hold only at its start, at thirty seconds and at its end.

items.title: Queue position demo
items.description: A working preview of Queue position.

items.name: coming-soon-state
items.title: Coming soon state
items.description: A placeholder for a feature that is not ready: what it will do, roughly when, and a button to be told when it launches.
items.docs: title gets the Soon badge, description says what the feature will do and expected completes "Planned for …". onNotify returns the promise of the sign-up: a rejection shows its message and the button comes back; success turns the button into "We will email you" (which takes the focus; after a rejection the button gets it back), remembered in localStorage under storageKey (default one per title). notified shows that state at once for people your server already knows. There is no countdown and no urgency. icon replaces the sparkle in the tile.

items.title: Coming soon state demo
items.description: A working preview of Coming soon state.

items.name: suspicious-activity-alert
items.title: Suspicious activity alert
items.description: A 'was this you?' alert for an unfamiliar sign-in, with device and place, and two clear answers: yes, or secure my account.
items.docs: event is { device, place, at, ip }: the IP address is hidden in part whatever you pass (203.0.x.x), and the place is called approximate. onConfirm (Yes, it was me) folds the alert away; onSecure (No, secure my account) runs and then shows the next steps, by default change your password and sign out other sessions. Pass steps with an href or an onSelect to make them buttons. Both callbacks may return promises and show a spinner, and a rejection is said in words. The alert is announced once as role="alert"; nothing takes the focus when it appears, the heading of the steps takes it after No, and a failed answer or step gives it back to the button that was pressed. defaultStep="secured" opens on the steps.

items.name: draft-restored-notice
items.title: Draft restored notice
items.description: Tells people their unsaved work came back after a crash or a closed tab: when it was saved, Keep or Start over, plus a useLocalDraft hook.
items.docs: DraftRestoredNotice takes savedAt, summary ("3 fields changed", "412 words"), timeZone and locale, onKeep, onDiscard (called after a second press of Start over) and onClosed (after it has folded away). It is a polite status, never an alert, and never takes the focus. useLocalDraft(key, value, { delay, enabled }) returns { draft, clear }: it saves value to localStorage a moment after the last change (and when the tab is hidden), reports a draft found on mount in draft (null on the server and on the first paint), never overwrites it before the form has changed, and clear() deletes it: call it after the form was saved for real, and from Start over. value must survive JSON.

items.title: Draft restored notice demo
items.description: A working preview of Draft restored notice.

items.name: unsupported-browser-notice
items.title: Unsupported browser notice
items.description: A calm notice for a browser that cannot run your app: what is missing in plain words, which browsers work, and Continue anyway.
items.docs: requires lists what the app needs: each entry has a label, shown when it is missing, and a test, either a function that returns false when the browser lacks it or data such as { css: "container-type: inline-size" } or { api: "IntersectionObserver" }, which also works from a Server Component. browsers lists the browsers that work, each with its name, minVersion and the official href. When the visitor's browser can be read from its user agent, is on the list and is older, the notice says so and its card shows the version it has. The checks run once the page is live, so the server renders nothing, and a browser that passes every check gets no notice and no gap. Continue anyway is always offered, is remembered for the session under storageKey and calls onContinue; dismissible adds a close button that hides it for this page view only and calls onDismiss. Above your content it pushes the page down once when it appears; give it className="fixed inset-x-4 bottom-4 z-50" to float it over the page instead, and add max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] overflow-y-auto if a screen can be shorter than the notice, so it scrolls instead of running off the top. userAgent overrides the visitor's own, for previews and tests. labels carries every word.

items.description: A working preview of Unsupported browser notice.

items.name: needs-setup-state
items.title: Needs setup state
items.description: Stands in for a feature that needs one step first: what is missing, why, the steps done and left, and the action that fixes it.
items.docs: title says what is needed, as the action it asks for, and description says why. steps is a list of { label, done }: a finished step shows a check and the word Done, the first open step is marked Next and carries aria-current="step", the rest are read out as not done, and a polite status says how many are finished. actionLabel and onAction make the main button; if onAction returns a promise the button shows a spinner and ignores presses until it settles, without losing focus. secondary is a node beside it, such as a link. minHeight is the height of the feature the panel stands in for, in pixels or any CSS length, so the page does not jump when setup finishes. icon replaces the plug. Use it for one missing prerequisite that blocks one specific thing, not for onboarding. labels carries every word.

items.description: A working preview of Needs setup state.

items.name: notice-stack
items.title: Notice stack
items.description: Several notices in one place: the most urgent on top, the rest folded under '+2 more', each closable on its own.
items.docs: notices is a list of { id, tone, title, body, action, dismissible } in any order: the stack sorts it by tone (error, warning, info) and keeps your order within a level. max (default 1) is how many show in full; the rest fold under a +N more button, whose name carries the count and which unfolds them in place. A dismissible notice has a close button that calls onDismiss(id); remove it from notices and the next one comes forward and takes focus. A notice that arrives after the first paint is announced politely, and an error is announced once, as an alert; what is there on load is not announced. Only errors use colour: a warning and information differ by icon, weight and the word read before the title. label names the region. labels carries every word.

items.description: A working preview of Notice stack.

items.name: streak-tracker
items.title: Streak tracker
items.description: A week of days with the streak count: filled for days done, ringed for today, hollow for what was missed.
items.docs: days lists the completed days as YYYY-MM-DD, and today is the day it is now: leave it out to read the browser's clock in timeZone once the page is live (until then the card holds its place with empty circles, so pass today when you render on the server). The count is the run of days in a row that ends today, or yesterday while today is still open, so it only falls to nothing after a whole day was missed. The week starts on weekStartsOn, or on the locale's own first weekday, and a page left open past midnight moves on to the new day by itself. Every day has a name that says its state in words, such as Tuesday, done, so nothing depends on colour, and missed days are plain empty circles, never red. With onDayClick the days that have come are buttons and receive { date, done, today }. The count is a status: it is read out when it changes and swells quietly when today is completed, unless motion is reduced. labels carries every word.

items.title: Streak tracker demo
items.description: A working preview of Streak tracker.

items.name: comment-composer
items.title: Comment composer
items.description: A comment box that stays one line until focused, then offers Cancel and Comment, sends with Cmd or Ctrl Enter and keeps the draft.
items.docs: value and onChange keep the text in your state, so a draft survives re-renders and route changes, and a box with text stays open; leave value out and it keeps its own. onSubmit receives the trimmed text and may return a promise: the button shows a spinner and keeps focus while it runs, the box clears when it resolves and goes back to its one line with the cursor still in it, and when it rejects the text is kept and an alert shows the error's message, or labels.failed. Comment stays disabled until there is text, Cmd or Ctrl Enter sends, Escape folds an empty box and Cancel throws the draft away. maxLength adds a count near the end, author gives the avatar, and disabled locks the box for a closed thread: say why in placeholder. It is a form of its own, so do not nest it in another form. labels carries every word.

items.title: Comment composer demo
items.description: A working preview of Comment composer.

items.name: document-upload-row
items.title: Document upload row
items.description: One requested document, such as a passport or proof of address, with its status, the chosen file and replace and remove, ready to stack.
items.docs: label names the document and description says what is accepted. status is missing, uploading, uploaded or attention; leave it out and it follows the file. progress, from 0 to 100, fills the bar while uploading, error is the reason shown when it needs attention, and file is what was provided, a File or the { name, size } your server kept; leave file out and the row remembers the one that was chosen. accept and maxSize are checked before onFileChange runs, and a file that fails is turned away with the reason. onFileChange receives the File, or null on Remove and Cancel, and is where you start the upload. required is said in words beside the name and keeps a form from submitting without a file: the row says what is missing and focus goes to its Choose file button. name keeps the real file input in the form for FormData and server actions, and a file can be dropped on the row. The status is a polite live region. labels carries every word.

items.name: document-upload-row-demo
items.title: Document upload row demo
items.description: A working preview of Document upload row.

items.name: image-upload-grid
items.title: Image upload grid
items.description: Manage the images of a product or a gallery: add tiles, mark the first as main, reorder with buttons or drag, and remove.
items.docs: images is the set to show, { id, src, alt }[], the first one the main image. The grid arranges and never uploads: files from the add tile, or dropped on the grid, pass the accept, maxSize and room checks and onFilesAdded receives those that passed; make an image of each (an object URL gives an instant preview), start the upload and put it in images. onImagesChange receives the new set after a move or a removal, by the buttons or by dragging a tile onto another. Each tile has Move earlier, Move later and Remove buttons, shown on hover and focus, always on a screen that cannot hover, and always reachable by keyboard. max shows the count as 5 of 8 and, once reached, switches the add tile off and says why. Moves, removals and additions are spoken, and focus stays on the button that was pressed. labels carries every word.

items.name: image-upload-grid-demo
items.title: Image upload grid demo
items.description: A working preview of Image upload grid.

items.name: image-alt-field
items.title: Image alt text field
items.description: Upload an image and describe it in the same place: a preview, an alt text box with live advice, and a decorative checkbox that is a deliberate choice.
items.docs: src is an image that already exists; a file the person chooses is previewed from the file itself and wins over it. value and onValueChange report { file, alt, decorative }, and defaultValue starts it when you do not control it. The decorative checkbox empties the description and switches the box off, and unchecking it brings the old text back, so decorative is a decision and not a field that was forgotten. The advice line under the box follows the text: empty, starting with image of or photo of, looking like a file name, very short, near maxLength, and fine. maxLength (125) limits the text and is counted. invalid shows a missing description as an error, and with required a missing image too; required also keeps a form from submitting without an image, and then the error shows and focus goes to Choose an image. accept and maxSize are checked before a file is taken, and name puts the file, the description (nameAlt) and the mark (nameDecorative) in the form. labels carries every word.

items.name: image-alt-field-demo
items.title: Image alt text field demo
items.description: A working preview of Image alt text field.

items.name: drop-overlay
items.title: Drop overlay
items.description: Let people drop files anywhere on a page or panel: an overlay appears the moment a file is dragged over it and says what will happen, or why not.
items.docs: Wrap a region (or pass global to take a drop anywhere in the window) and give it onFiles. While files are dragged over, an overlay with a dashed frame, an icon and message (default Drop files to upload) fills the region; it follows the radius and border you give the wrapper. Enter and leave are counted, so children never make it flicker, and dragged text and links are ignored. accept takes the same rules as the input (image/*,.pdf): the drag is judged by type from dataTransfer.items, and when none of the dragged files can match, the overlay shows rejectMessage and the drop is not allowed. Types that are ambiguous between platforms (a .csv is often application/vnd.ms-excel) and files whose type the browser does not reveal are never refused during the drag. The drop is checked exactly, by name and type: matching files go to onFiles, the others to onReject. The message is spoken as a polite status. The overlay is not a place to click, so pair it with a file button (the File trigger or your own) for the keyboard and for anyone who does not drag. DropOverlayPanel is the overlay itself, exported for previews, and labels carries the words under the message.

items.name: drop-overlay-demo
items.title: Drop overlay demo
items.description: A working preview of Drop overlay.

items.name: form-actions
items.title: Form actions
items.description: The button row that ends a form: primary last, Cancel beside it, a destructive action kept apart, a pending state, a hint and an optional sticky bar.
items.docs: primary is the main button (label, onClick, type, disabled) and is last in the DOM, so Tab finishes on it; secondary is the quiet one beside it (usually Cancel) and never submits; start is a slot at the far start for an action of another kind, such as Delete project. pending switches every button off together, shows a spinner on the primary without changing its label, sets aria-busy on the row and tells a screen reader once (labels.pending). The browser drops the focus of a button that is switched off, so the row gives it back to the primary when the wait ends. hint is a polite live region for a line such as Unsaved changes. align places the buttons at the end (default) or the start, sticky pins the row to the bottom of its scroll container with a hairline above and safe-area padding, and under 480px of the row's own width the buttons stack at full width with the primary on top (a visual order: Tab still goes Cancel, then the primary). From 480px up the row wraps rather than squeezes: the hint keeps the width of its words, and what does not fit goes to a line of its own. shortcut makes Command or Control plus Enter press the primary from anywhere in the form, also in a textarea: on (default), hint (also shows the keys on the button) or off. The press is a click on the primary, so onClick, native validation and the form's onSubmit all run as for a mouse press.

items.name: form-actions-demo
items.title: Form actions demo
items.description: A working preview of Form actions.

items.name: form-section
items.title: Form section
items.description: A fieldset with a legend, help text and a Required or Optional note, stacked or split into a sticky title column and a card of fields.
items.docs: title is the legend, so a screen reader names the group before the first field; description and the requirement note (required or optional) describe it through aria-describedby. layout is stacked (title above the fields, the default) or split (title and help in a left column that is sticky on wide screens, the fields in a bordered card on the right); both are one column below 48rem of the section's own width, so also at 320px. error is a problem with the group as a whole: it renders above the fields with role alert and is tied to the fieldset; errors of one field belong to that field. disabled is the native fieldset attribute and switches off every control inside, the footer included; only the title is dimmed, because the note and the help beside it say why. footer is a slot for a section-level action such as Save. divided (default true) draws a hairline and a fixed space above every section after the first, so sections placed one after another read as one column. The legend is floated: that makes it an ordinary box beside the fields instead of the browser's special one on the border, and the fieldset contains the float. labels carries the words Required and Optional.

items.name: form-section-demo
items.title: Form section demo
items.description: A working preview of Form section.

items.name: translatable-field
items.title: Translatable field
items.description: One field in many languages: a tab per language with a clear missing mark, so editors see what is translated and what is not.
items.docs: locales is the list of { code, label }; defaultLocale (default: the first) is the source language: it is moved to the front, it is what required applies to and what Copy from copies from. value is a record such as { en: "Welcome", nl: "Welkom" } and onValueChange gets the whole record on every change; a language that is emptied loses its key. Each tab says where its language stands in an icon and words: a check when filled, a dash and Missing when empty, Required for the default language when required is set, or Over limit; the tabs wrap onto a second line when the languages do not fit, and a screen reader hears each as its code, its language and where it stands (NL, Nederlands filled), so a voice command that says the code on show finds the tab. maxLength is a guide and not a wall (a German translation is often longer than its English source): a longer text is allowed, counted in red and marked on its tab. A line above the tabs says how many languages are filled. In any other language the default text is shown above the field with a Copy from English button that fills the field and offers Undo for a few seconds. The tabs use manual activation: arrow keys move focus between them, Enter, Space or a click chooses one and the focus goes into the field, ready to write in that language. locale and onLocaleChange let several fields on one form follow the same language. With name, each language also goes out in a hidden input called name[code]; a hidden input has no native required check, so validate required in your schema and set invalid to show the result. labels carries every word.

items.name: translatable-field-demo
items.title: Translatable field demo
items.description: A working preview of Translatable field.

items.name: utm-builder
items.title: UTM link builder
items.description: Build a tracked link: a base URL plus source, medium and campaign, with the result live, encoded and ready to copy.
items.docs: value holds the page and the tags ({ url, source, medium, campaign, term, content }; any you leave out are empty), with defaultValue and onValueChange for the uncontrolled and the reporting side. The link is built live: the page keeps its own parameters and its #fragment, every tag is encoded with encodeURIComponent (a space is %20), tags go in a fixed order, and a utm_ tag already in the address is replaced instead of doubled. Source, medium and campaign are required, term only with requireTerm and content never (it is marked Optional). suggestions gives the names your team already uses, shown as chips under each tag so naming stays consistent; the defaults are a few common sources and mediums. A value with capitals or spaces gets a quiet warning in words (Reports treat Email and email as different sources) and a one-click fix that lower-cases it and puts hyphens for spaces. An address without a scheme is explained and fixed in a click, and an address that is not http or https is refused. The result is a status that settles after typing pauses, and onLinkChange reports the finished link, or null while it is incomplete, at the same moment. baseUrl fills the address and locks it, for when the page is chosen elsewhere. name adds a hidden input with the finished link. locale is for the lists in messages and labels carries every word.

items.name: utm-builder-demo
items.title: UTM link builder demo
items.description: A working preview of UTM link builder.

items.name: status-message-field
items.title: Status message field
items.description: Set what you are up to: a short status with an icon, quick presets such as In a meeting, and when it should clear itself.
items.docs: A text input with a glyph button on its left that opens a menu of presets, and a Clear after select (the house Select) under it. Choosing a preset fills the text, the icon and its usual clear time; the focus then goes to the text, so it can be edited. presets is a list of { id, text, icon, clearAfter } where icon is the name of one of sixteen glyphs (calendar, target, palm-tree, thermometer, car, coffee, headphones, laptop, home, plane, phone, utensils, moon, book, bike, dumbbell) and clearAfter the id of a clear option, so a status can come straight from a server. clearOptions is a list of { id, label, minutes } or { id, label, until: today | week }; the defaults are Don't clear, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, Today and This week. onValueChange(value, clearsAt) reports { text, icon, clearAfter } and the moment it clears as an ISO timestamp, counted from now (or the moment of the change) in timeZone: Today ends at that zone midnight and This week at the coming Monday midnight, daylight saving included. The preview shows the status as it will appear next to displayName, with the time it clears in locale and timeZone; pass now for a stable preview. A status with an icon and no text is allowed. name submits the text as name, plus nameIcon and nameClearAfter. labels carries every word.

items.name: status-message-field-demo
items.title: Status message field demo
items.description: A working preview of Status message field.

items.name: focal-point-field
items.title: Focal point field
items.description: Mark the part of an image that must never be cropped: click or drag a point and see square, wide and tall crops that keep it in view.
items.docs: The image carries a crosshair handle that works like a two-axis slider: click or drag anywhere on the picture, or focus the handle and use the arrow keys (1%, Shift 10%) and Home to centre it. step is the unit in percent: the point snaps to its multiples and the keys move by it, Shift by ten times as much. The handle is role slider and says its place as 45% across, 30% down (labels.position). Beside the image, previews (default square, wide 16:9 and tall 3:4; pass your own { label, ratio } list) show the same picture cropped with object-position set to the point, side by side at one height (a row that is full wraps to the next, and a very narrow shape keeps a width a crop can be judged at), so the result is seen before saving. onValueChange reports { x, y } as numbers from 0 to 100, ready for object-position: ${x}% ${y}%; value and defaultValue control it. Pointer events make it work with mouse, touch and pen, and a handle grabbed by its edge does not jump to the pointer. The image is shown as large as fits in 26rem of height; while it loads there is a skeleton, and an image that fails shows a calm error with the reason and a Try again button. name submits the point as nameX and nameY. labels carries every word.

items.name: focal-point-field-demo
items.title: Focal point field demo
items.description: A working preview of Focal point field.

items.name: image-cropper
items.title: Image cropper
items.description: Choose the crop of a photo: drag it under a fixed frame, zoom with a slider or the keys, lock an aspect ratio and get the rectangle back.
items.docs: The frame keeps the shape you chose and stays in the middle; the picture moves under it. Drag the picture, zoom with the slider, the plus and minus buttons or keys, a two-finger pinch or Ctrl and the wheel (a notch zooms by about a third); what is outside the frame is dimmed. onValueChange reports { x, y, width, height, zoom } with the rectangle in the picture's own pixels (rounded to two decimals; round before a server cuts with them) and zoom 1 meaning the largest crop of that shape, 2 half as wide. value and defaultValue control it; value null means none yet and the cropper reports the centred one. It also reports once when the picture has loaded and whenever a change of aspect or shape makes a new crop, keeping the middle and the zoom. aspect is a number (1, 4 / 3, 16 / 9) or free, which shows handles on the frame's edges and corners to drag (the frame settles back to fill the stage when the hand lets go); shape round is a circle for avatars. minZoom (at least 1) and maxZoom (default 4) limit the zoom. The frame is the keyboard target and a slider for assistive technology: arrow keys move the crop 1% of the picture (Shift 10%), plus and minus zoom, Home resets, Alt and the arrow keys resize a free frame, and the place is announced as 40% from the left, 25% from the top, zoom 150%. Reset restores the centred fit. A picture that fails to load shows an error with the reason (offline, not an image, or a bad address) and Try again. onReady hands over the loaded image element; cropToBlob(image, crop, { type, quality, maxWidth, shape }), imported from the item's crop module (@rhs-ui/application/image-cropper/crop), cuts the crop out in the browser and returns a Blob (round gives transparent corners, use PNG or WebP). A picture from another site needs crossOrigin anonymous and CORS headers, or the browser refuses the cut. labels carries every word.

items.name: image-cropper-demo
items.title: Image cropper demo
items.description: A working preview of Image cropper.

items.name: conditional-fields
items.title: Conditional fields
items.description: A checkbox, switch or radio that reveals its own fields when chosen: the reveal is announced, and hidden fields are inert and left out of the submit.
items.docs: Put the fields inside; they open beneath the control when it is on. trigger is checkbox (the default), switch or radio. A checkbox or switch can keep its own state (defaultChecked) or be controlled (checked and onCheckedChange). A radio sits inside your RadioGroup and gets checked={value === "its value"}, because the group owns the choice. The control carries aria-controls (and aria-expanded on a checkbox or switch, the roles that may have it), and a polite status says that fields appeared or went. Closed, the fields are inert and in a disabled fieldset: Tab skips them, a screen reader does not find them and the form does not send them. keepValues (default true) keeps what was typed while the panel is shut; false removes the fields after the fold, so uncontrolled inputs start over. Focus never moves into the panel by itself. Each panel is a fieldset named by the label, so a ConditionalFields inside another one is a nested level.

items.name: conditional-fields-demo
items.title: Conditional fields demo
items.description: A working preview of Conditional fields.

items.name: field-repeater
items.title: Field repeater
items.description: An 'Add another' group of fields that repeats row by row, with add, remove, a minimum and maximum, and focus that lands in the new row.
items.docs: Give it value and onChange (or defaultValue, and the text stays in uncontrolled inputs), a createItem that makes a row with a new id every time, and a renderRow that draws the fields of one row. The third argument of renderRow has the row's number, its name ("Contact 2") and update(patch). Rows are keyed by item.id, so typed text stays with its row when a row above is removed. After Add, focus lands on the first field of the new row; after Remove, on the row that took its place, or on Add when none is left. A polite status says "Contact 3 added" or "Contact 2 removed". At max, Add is off and says why; at min, Remove is not shown; an empty list is one dashed Add row. itemLabel, itemsLabel, addLabel and labels carry the words.

items.name: field-repeater-demo
items.title: Field repeater demo
items.description: A working preview of Field repeater.

items.name: form-dialog
items.title: Form dialog
items.description: A dialog that is a form: Enter submits, buttons lock while it saves, closing is blocked mid-save and a failed save keeps everything typed.
items.docs: Pass the fields as children, each with a name, and an onSubmit that gets the FormData and may return a promise. Native validation runs first. While the promise is pending the fields, Cancel and the close button are disabled, Escape and the backdrop do nothing, and the save button stays focusable and says it is busy. A rejection puts its message in an alert at the top of the body and keeps everything typed; a resolution closes the dialog and focus returns to the trigger (pass trigger, or focus goes back to whatever had it). Focus starts on the first field. With dirtyGuard, closing a changed form asks "Discard changes?" in the footer, with Keep editing focused; changes are found by comparing the named fields with what they held when the dialog opened. open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control it from outside. labels translates the words.

items.name: form-dialog-demo
items.title: Form dialog demo
items.description: A working preview of Form dialog.

items.name: form-tabs
items.title: Form tabs
items.description: A long form split across tabs that still submits as one: errors show on the tab, and a field inside a hidden panel is revealed before it is focused.
items.docs: Put FormTabs inside your form. Every panel stays in the page, so one form sends everything and values survive a switch of tab. When a submit fails the browser cannot focus a field in a hidden panel and stays silent; FormTabs takes the first invalid field over, opens its tab, focuses it and asks the browser to point at it. A tab with problems says "Pricing, 2 problems" with the number beside the name, and a thin line under the tabs fills with the share of tabs that are clean. Problems are counted from the browser's own validation (required, pattern, min) once a submit fails, and update as fields are fixed. Pass errorCounts, keyed by tab id, for what only your server knows; it wins for the tabs it names. value and onValueChange control the tab. In a narrow form (under 19 rem) the tabs tighten so three with a count still fit; when they do not, the strip scrolls, fades at the end that has more and brings the tab that opens into view, also when a failed submit opened it. A field in a hidden Radix Select is not focusable: put required on text-like inputs.

items.name: form-tabs-demo
items.title: Form tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Form tabs.

items.name: editable-section
items.title: Editable section
items.description: View or edit a group of details in place: a summary with an Edit button turns into fields with Save and Cancel, and focus returns when done.
items.docs: Pass the facts as view (a DescriptionList is made for it) and the fields as children, each with a name. Edit swaps one for the other and moves focus to the first field; Escape cancels and focus lands on the Edit button; Save returns there too, after a polite "Saved". onSave gets the FormData and may return a promise: the fields and Cancel lock while it runs, the save button says it is busy, and a rejection keeps the form open with the message in an alert and everything as typed. Changed fields make Cancel and Escape ask "Discard changes?" in place; dirty overrides the automatic check. editing, defaultEditing and onEditingChange control it, and disabled switches the Edit button off so that other sections wait while one is open. The edit form is a real form: do not put the section inside another one. The Edit button is named "Edit" plus the title.

items.name: editable-section-demo
items.title: Editable section demo
items.description: A working preview of Editable section.

items.name: danger-zone
items.title: Danger zone
items.description: The destructive actions of a settings page in one clearly marked section, each with its consequence in words and a confirm step.
items.docs: Give it actions: id, title, description (the consequence, in words), label (the button), onConfirm (which may return a promise) and optionally confirmation, the name to type before the confirm button works. Each button opens an alert dialog that restates what will happen, with Cancel focused; the dialog stays open while onConfirm runs and shows its rejection in an alert. disabledReason switches a row off and writes the reason under its description, because a disabled button cannot say it. The destructive tone is only in the border and the button labels, and the heading says "Danger zone" in words. dialogTitle, dialogDescription and confirmLabel adjust the dialog; the description in the dialog is plain text or inline elements. labels translates the words.

items.name: danger-zone-demo
items.title: Danger zone demo
items.description: A working preview of Danger zone.

items.name: contact-fieldset
items.title: Contact fieldset
items.description: Contact details for a checkout or enquiry: first and last name, email and phone with country code, with autofill tokens and per-field errors.
items.docs: A fieldset with first and last name side by side (stacked on a phone), email, a phone number with its country code and an optional company line. value (or defaultValue) and onValueChange carry { firstName, lastName, email, phone, company }; the email comes back trimmed and in lower case and the phone number in E.164. A number typed, pasted or filled in with its country code ("+31 6 1234 5678", "0031 6 1234 5678", "+44 7911 123456") picks that country and the field keeps the national number, so it is never stored under the wrong code; the (0) after a code is dropped. A code that is not in the list leaves the value empty and says "Pick the country in the list and leave out the +." when the field is left (unknownCountry in labels). Inputs carry given-name, family-name, email and organization autocomplete tokens with type and inputMode; the phone field's token is tel-national because the country code is its own control. Fields are checked when left, not on every keystroke, and a message goes the moment the problem is fixed. errors adds your own, required lists the required fields, showCompany adds the company line, and disabled switches the whole group off. The phone value that is sent is a hidden input named phone. Nothing is sent anywhere.

items.name: contact-fieldset-demo
items.title: Contact fieldset demo
items.description: A working preview of Contact fieldset.

items.name: social-links-fieldset
items.title: Social links fieldset
items.description: Profile links with each network's address pre-filled: paste a full URL and it is cut down to the handle, then checked.
items.docs: Pass networks (id, label, prefix, pattern, message) and value (or defaultValue) with onValueChange: the value is { website, [networkId]: handle }. Each network is an input group with its prefix in a cell of its own, so people type only the handle. A pasted link to that network is cut down to the handle on the spot, a leading @ is stripped, and a pattern check on blur says what is wrong in the network's message. The website takes anything that parses as an http or https address and adds https:// when it is missing. Only what passed leaves the fieldset: onValueChange, and the hidden input each field sends under its name, hold a handle that matches its pattern, a website that is an http or https address, or an empty string, never the text that failed, so a value is safe to use as a link. The text stays in the field until it is fixed, with the message beside it. What you pass as value or defaultValue is shown as given, not checked. The browser can be bypassed: cleanSocialLinks(networks, input), toHandle, checkHandle and toWebsite are exported from social-links-fieldset/links, a module without "use client", so a server can run the same check on what was posted. Optional rows say "Optional". A pattern can be a RegExp or its source as a string; from a Server Component pass the string. Networks are named in text, never with logos. errors adds your own messages. Nothing is sent anywhere.

items.name: social-links-fieldset-demo
items.title: Social links fieldset demo
items.description: A working preview of Social links fieldset.

items.name: answers-review
items.title: Answers review
items.description: Check your answers before sending: grouped answers in a summary list, each with a Change link and a clear Not provided marker.
items.docs: Pass groups (title, rows of key, label, value, files, href or onChange, error). Each group is a section with a heading and a real description list. A row with an href gets a Change link; otherwise it calls its own onChange or the review's onChange(key). A row with no answer says "Not provided" in muted text and offers Add instead of Change. Text keeps its line breaks and long words wrap; files are listed by name. Every link says "Change" and then the question, for screen readers, and is described by the row's error when there is one, so the page can be where a blocked submit gets fixed. headingLevel sets the section titles; emptyText and labels carry the words. It has no hooks of its own, so a Server Component can render it when every row has an href.

items.name: answers-review-demo
items.title: Answers review demo
items.description: A working preview of Answers review.

items.name: form-outline
items.title: Form outline
items.description: The jump list of a long form: each section with Done, Needs attention or Not started in shape and text, the one in view marked as you scroll.
items.docs: sections is the list: each has an id (the id of an element on the page), a label, a status (done, attention or todo) and, for attention, an errorCount that is written as "2 problems". By default the outline follows the scroll, in the page or in whatever scrolling container holds the sections, and marks the section in view with aria-current="location"; pass activeId to decide it yourself, or defaultActiveId to choose where it starts. Following a link scrolls the section to scrollOffset px under the top of the view (smoothly, at once under reduced motion) and moves focus to its first heading, which is made focusable by script; onNavigate receives the id first. sticky (default true) keeps the list in the side column, at lg:top-6 which className can change, and on a phone pins the compact bar to the top, where its own height is added to scrollOffset. The bar says "Section 3 of 6", shows the problem count of the current section and opens the list as a panel; Escape or a press outside closes it. A thin Progress counts the sections done. The nav is a landmark labelled "Form sections" (label), and labels renames every word.

items.name: form-outline-demo
items.title: Form outline demo
items.description: A working preview of Form outline.

items.name: status-select
items.title: Status select
items.description: Pick a status where the shape tells the state, not the colour: a marker and a word per option, grouped into open and closed, in a compact trigger.
items.docs: statuses is the list: value, label, kind (backlog, todo, progress, review, done or cancelled; leave it out when you pass a marker) and an optional group. Options with the same group are listed together under a quiet heading, in the order the groups first appear. The six markers are drawn on a 16 unit grid and differ in shape, not only in weight; marker replaces one with your own 16px drawing, so the same select can show a stage or a priority. The list is the house Select: arrow keys, Home and End, typeahead on the words, Escape returns focus. showShortcuts writes 1 to 9 beside the first nine options and lets the number keys pick them while the list is open. size sm with variant ghost is the compact trigger for a table cell or a detail panel. The trigger shows the marker and the word, and a screen reader hears the group after them ("In progress, Open"). Name the trigger with aria-label, or with a Label whose htmlFor is its id. name and required make it a form field.

items.name: status-select-demo
items.title: Status select demo
items.description: A working preview of Status select.

items.name: guest-picker
items.title: Guest picker
items.description: Adults, children and infants in one popover: a stepper for each, ages as help text, and limits that explain themselves in words when they stop a button.
items.docs: groups is the list of kinds of guest: id, label, description, min, max, noun ({ one, other } for the summary) and countsTowardTotal (false for infants). value and onValueChange speak a number per group id, such as { adults: 2, children: 1, infants: 0 }. maxTotal caps the guests that count; the summary on the button reads "2 adults, 1 child" (formatSummary writes it differently). Minus and plus are real buttons named after the kind ("Fewer adults"); they are aria-disabled, never disabled, so they keep focus, and a stopped button points at the line that says why: under the row for a limit of its own (at least one adult), in the footer when the total is full ("The limit is 6 guests in total. Infants are not counted."). The number between them is a spin button you can type into and step with the arrow keys, Home and End. Every change is announced politely. Escape closes the panel with focus back on the button. commit="done" keeps the steps in the panel until Done is pressed, and closing any other way throws them away. open, defaultOpen (which does not take focus) and onOpenChange control the panel; labels renames every word; the button takes id and the usual button props.

items.name: likert-matrix
items.title: Likert matrix
items.description: Several statements on one scale: a real table with one tab stop per row, a sticky statement column, and one card per statement on a phone.
items.docs: statements are the rows (id, text) and options the shared scale, first point first: a plain word is its own label and value, { value, label } keeps them apart. value maps a statement id to the chosen option value. The layout follows the width of its container, not the screen: from 36rem it is a real table with the scale as visible column headers in equal columns, each statement a row header and one point per cell; below that it is one card per statement with the scale as a vertical radio list. In the table every point is a radio named by its statement and its column, each row has one tab stop, and the arrow keys, Home and End move and choose inside it; the table scrolls inside its own frame with the statement column held in place. requireAll makes a form the grid sits in refuse to submit until every statement is answered: focus goes to the first that is not, those rows say "Choose one" in text, and an error lists them with a link to each. showErrors does the same for a submit of your own. name sends one field per statement, <name>.<statement id>. legend names the table and the list of cards, labels renames every word.

items.title: Likert matrix demo
items.description: A working preview of Likert matrix.

items.name: answer-checklist
items.title: Answer checklist
items.description: A checklist where each item gets an answer, Pass, Fail or N/A, or Yes and No, with a note that opens on the answers that need explaining.
items.docs: items are the statements (id, label, hint, notePlaceholder) and options the answers: value, label and an optional tone (pass, fail or skip) that sets the shape of the mark; the default is Pass, Fail and Not applicable. value maps a statement id to { answer, note }, and onValueChange receives the whole map. noteOn lists the answers that need a note: choosing one opens a required textarea under the row, and the row stays open, marked "Note required", until it has text; the note is kept if the answer changes. Each row is a radio group (the house segmented control) named by its statement and hint, and shows its state in a mark and in words. The header counts what is left ("7 of 12 answered, 1 note missing") in a polite live region next to a thin Progress, and Jump to next unanswered moves focus to the first open row: to its answer, or to its empty note. On a phone the control wraps under the statement at full width. labels renames every word.

items.name: answer-checklist-demo
items.title: Answer checklist demo
items.description: A working preview of Answer checklist.

items.name: event-time-fieldset
items.title: Event time fieldset
items.description: When does it happen: start and end date and time, an All day switch, and an end that moves with the start so the length is kept.
items.docs: value is { start, end, allDay }: start and end are wall-clock text, "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm" (or "" while nothing is chosen), read in timeZone, so the same value means the same on every machine; convert to an instant with the zone when you save. Moving the start moves the end by the same amount, so a one-hour meeting stays one hour, and a start picked with no end yet gets an hour. An end at or before the start (a later day for all-day events, on or after the first) is refused with the reason in words, in an alert, and the old end stays; it is not reported. All day hides the times and keeps them, so turning it off brings them back. A sentence in a polite live region says the whole event: "Tue 27 Oct, 14:00 to 15:00 (1 h), Europe/Amsterdam". minuteStep sets the times in the list, minDate ("YYYY-MM-DD") the first day, locale the language of the dates. The pickers are the house Date picker and Time picker; start and end are each a group named "Starts" and "Ends", inside a fieldset with a legend. labels renames every word.

items.name: event-time-fieldset-demo
items.title: Event time fieldset demo
items.description: A working preview of Event time fieldset.

items.name: send-schedule-field
items.title: Send schedule field
items.description: Send now or later: two choices, a day and time that open for later, the time zone in words, and a sentence saying exactly when it goes out.
items.docs: value is { mode, at }: mode is "now" or "later", and at is an ISO time with an offset ("2026-10-27T09:00:00+01:00"), or null while the day or the time is missing or was refused. The two choices are a real radio group, so the arrow keys move and choose. Schedule opens the house Date time picker, read in timeZone (an IANA name; the offset comes from the zone at that moment, daylight saving included). A time sooner than now plus minLeadMinutes is refused with a message that names the earliest time that works, and is reported as at: null so a Send button can wait. A sentence in a polite live region always says the result: "Goes out Tue 27 Oct at 09:00, Europe/Amsterdam, in 3 days". now fixes the clock for tests and previews; without it the field reads the browser clock after the page has loaded, so the server and the browser agree, and again every half minute. minuteStep sets the times in the list, locale the language of the dates and of "in 3 days", labels renames every word.

items.title: Send schedule field demo
items.description: A working preview of Send schedule field.

items.name: quiet-hours-field
items.title: Quiet hours field
items.description: Do not disturb on a schedule: a switch, from and to times, the days it applies to, and a sentence that understands overnight ranges.
items.docs: value is { enabled, from, to, days }: from and to are "HH:MM" in 24-hour time, and days are getDay() numbers (0 is Sunday) naming the days a quiet period starts on. A range that crosses midnight (22:00 to 07:00) is valid: the field says so, and a thin 24-hour track shows where the quiet falls in two pieces. From equal to To is refused with a message, and so is turning off the last day; a refused change is never reported. The days are toggle chips named by the whole weekday, in the language of locale, in a row that starts on weekStartsOn (default Monday). A sentence in a polite live region says the schedule, "Quiet from 22:00 to 07:00, Monday to Friday". Switching it off dims and locks the rest but clears nothing, so switching it on again brings the old schedule back. minuteStep sets the times in the list, disabled turns the whole field off, and labels renames every word, including the ones in the sentences.

items.name: quiet-hours-field-demo
items.title: Quiet hours field demo
items.description: A working preview of Quiet hours field.

items.name: inherited-field
items.title: Inherited field
items.description: A setting that follows its parent until you override it: the inherited value shown and named, an Override switch, and Reset back to inherited.
items.docs: Pass the parent's value and who it comes from as inherited ({ value, source }), the person's own value as value (null while the setting follows the parent, which is also what onValueChange reports, so a form can send it as no value) and control, a function that renders your input from the value, onValueChange and the ids it is handed: spread them onto the input. The control is not rendered while the value is inherited, so a form never sends it. The Override switch starts the control from the inherited value, or from the value the person had before; Reset and the switch go back, and the typed value is remembered until the field unmounts, so key it after a save; a value equal to the inherited one is not worth remembering and is not (equals compares objects and arrays, default Object.is). format writes a value in words ("30 days"), description adds a line under the label, and labels translates the fixed words. error marks the control invalid (aria-invalid on what your control spreads it onto) and shows the message; Input and Select draw that themselves, while a control that frames itself on a wrapper, like NumberInput, needs has-[input[aria-invalid=true]]:border-destructive on its className.

items.name: inherited-field-demo
items.title: Inherited field demo
items.description: A working preview of Inherited field.

items.name: agreement-scroll
items.title: Agreement scroll
items.description: Terms in a scrolling box with a read-progress line; the accept checkbox unlocks at the end, and keyboard users and short texts still work.
items.docs: Pass title, version and the text as children (h4, p, ol and ul are styled). The checkbox stays disabled until the reader reaches the end of the scrolling region, or at once when the text fits; once reached it stays unlocked, and a text that is already accepted can always be un-accepted. Control it with accepted and onAcceptedChange, or defaultAccepted. requireScroll={false} offers the text without the lock and hides the hint, the percentage and the jump button. The region is focusable and named by the title, so the arrow keys, Page Up and Down, Space and End scroll it; Jump to the end scrolls there (instantly under reduced motion) and hands the focus to the checkbox. A ResizeObserver checks again when the width changes. height sets the region's height (default 16rem), acceptLabel the words by the checkbox, name submits it with a form, and labels translates the fixed words.

items.name: agreement-scroll-demo
items.title: Agreement scroll demo
items.description: A working preview of Agreement scroll.

items.name: report-form
items.title: Report form
items.description: Report a post, a listing or a user: a short list of reasons, a detail box that opens when it helps, and clear words on what happens next.
items.docs: Give it reasons ({ id, label, description, requiresDetail }), the subject being reported ({ kind, title, byline }) and onSubmit, which receives { reasonId, detail, block }; return a promise and the button shows it is working, and if it rejects the form stays and says so. A reason with requiresDetail opens a text box with a counter (maxDetail, default 500) and Send waits for minDetail characters (default 10); the line beside Send says what is missing. blockOption adds an 'Also block this user' checkbox, unticked, with your own words if you pass them. After a successful send a confirmation replaces the form, is announced politely and takes the focus; onDone adds its button, onCancel the Cancel button. value, defaultValue and onValueChange hold a draft ({ reasonId, detail, block }). In a Dialog, pass your DialogHeader as header so its title names the dialog; it stays in the page, unseen, after the report is sent, so the dialog keeps its name. In a Dialog that is shorter than the form, the subject, reasons and note scroll between the heading and the Send row, which both stay in view (the form is capped at the screen height less the dialog's margin and its default padding; elsewhere, give it a max-height with className and it scrolls the same way). labels translates the words.

items.name: report-form-demo
items.title: Report form demo
items.description: A working preview of Report form.

items.name: tiered-rates-editor
items.title: Tiered rates editor
items.description: Edit price breaks, shipping bands or commission tiers: ranges that chain automatically, so there are never gaps or overlaps.
items.docs: Pass the tiers as value ([{ from, rate }], first to last) with onValueChange. A tier ends one below where the next begins, so the To column is worked out and never typed, and the last row says 'and up'. The first tier starts where yours does and stays; every other From must lie between its neighbours, and a number that would make a tier end before it starts is refused with the reason in words: the cell keeps its last good number. A start is judged when typing pauses, when the cell is left and on Enter, so a number on its way ('7' before '75') is never refused; only one that more digits cannot repair (above the next tier's start) is refused at once. The reason replaces the note under the table while it is shown, and the band is kept as tall as the longest reason needs, so nothing moves. Below 20rem of width the Tier column is left out (the fields keep their names by row) so the table fits a small phone. Add appends a tier at a round number about twice the last start, with no rate yet; removing a tier hands its range to the one before it (the first tier's range goes to the next). With a currency the rate is money in minor units (cents), without one a plain number with rateSuffix after it. unit takes a word or { one, other }, rateLabel names the column and starts the note, minRows and maxRows limit the table, and labels translates the words.

items.name: tiered-rates-editor-demo
items.title: Tiered rates editor demo
items.description: A working preview of Tiered rates editor.

items.name: transfer-list
items.title: Transfer list
items.description: Move items between Available and Chosen: two searchable listboxes, add and remove buttons, double-click or Enter, counts, and moves that are announced.
items.docs: Pass items ({ id, label, description, disabled }) and control the chosen ids with value and onValueChange (new items are added at the end), or use defaultValue. Each list is a multi-select listbox with its own search and a header checkbox: click or Space toggles an item, Shift with click or the arrows selects a range, Control A selects all, and Enter or a double click moves the item, or the whole selection when it is part of it. Add, Add all, Remove and Remove all are disabled when they would do nothing; while a search is on, 'all' means what is shown. After a move the cursor stands where the items were and the move is announced; moved items are tinted for a moment. Disabled items cannot be moved. titles names the lists, name sends one hidden input per chosen id, height sizes them, labels translates the words. Below 42rem of container width the lists stack and the buttons lie in a row, each with its word under the chevron. The row under the cursor wears a ring only for keyboard focus; a click shows the selection tint alone.

items.name: transfer-list-demo
items.title: Transfer list demo
items.description: A working preview of Transfer list.

items.name: record-lookup
items.title: Record lookup
items.description: Pick one record from a big table: a field with a Look up button that opens a searchable, sortable, paged table in a dialog, loaded from your server.
items.docs: Give it columns ({ key, label, sortable, align, width }) and loadRows(query, signal), which answers { rows, total } for { search, page, pageSize, sort }, so the data can stay on the server. Each new question aborts the one before it, and a late answer is dropped even when your loader ignores the signal. Control the chosen record with value and onValueChange ({ id, plus a value per column key }; null when cleared). The field shows the record named by labelKey (the first column) with a muted line from detailKey (the second). In the dialog, Arrow Down moves from the search field into the rows, Enter in the field takes the chosen row or the first result, and Enter or a double click on a row takes it. title names the dialog, pageSize sets the rows, name sends the id with a form, labels translates the words. A width on any column (a CSS length, '12rem') fixes the layout, so the columns keep their places from one answer to the next and a long value is cut with an ellipsis; a column without a width shares what is left, and without any widths the table fits its columns to what it shows. The table keeps the room of a whole page so the dialog does not change height, and on a short screen it gives way and scrolls inside itself, so the paging, Select and Cancel are never covered. RecordLookupPanel is the same table without the dialog.

items.title: Record lookup demo
items.description: A working preview of Record lookup.

items.name: seo-fieldset
items.title: SEO fieldset
items.description: Page title and description fields with a live search-result preview and a length meter that turns to words before text would be cut off.
items.docs: Give it baseUrl and control it with value ({ title, description, slug }) and onValueChange, or defaultValue. Lengths are counted in characters as a person sees them (an emoji is one) after runs of spaces are collapsed, against titleLimit (60) and descriptionLimit (160); titleMin (30) and descriptionMin (70) start the recommended range. The meter turns to 'Too long, cut off at 60' with a warning icon, and only a change of state is announced, never every keystroke. The preview cuts the text after exactly the limit and closes it with an ellipsis; an empty field shows fallbackTitle or fallbackDescription in grey, so it is never blank. The address line is built from baseUrl and the slug; editSlug adds a field for the slug, tidied to lower case and hyphens when you leave it. name sends the fields with a form, locale sets how characters are counted, labels translates the words.

items.name: seo-fieldset-demo
items.title: SEO fieldset demo
items.description: A working preview of SEO fieldset.

items.name: chapter-list
items.title: Chapter list
items.description: The chapters of a video or podcast as timestamps: the playing one marked with a rail and a progress line, click to seek, each length shown.
items.docs: Pass chapters ({ start, title }, start in seconds), currentTime and onSeek; duration gives the last chapter an end and a length. Ends and lengths are worked out from the next start, so you only keep starts. The chapter that holds currentTime gets aria-current, a thin rail, a heavier title, a line that fills as the chapter goes by and "Now playing" for screen readers. Every row is a button read as one phrase ("04:12, Pricing, 3 minutes") that calls onSeek(start). Tab enters the list once, on the playing chapter; the arrow keys, Home and End walk it. The list moves itself to the playing chapter, never the page, and jumps without animation under reduced motion. It does not own the media element, so it works with a video, an audio element or an embed. maxHeight sets where it scrolls, locale writes the lengths, labels translates the fixed words.

items.name: chapter-list-demo
items.title: Chapter list demo
items.description: A working preview of Chapter list.

items.name: media-playlist
items.title: Media playlist
items.description: Tracks or videos for your own player: a now-playing row with an animated equaliser, durations, an Up next heading and arrow-key browsing.
items.docs: Pass items ({ id, title, subtitle?, duration, artwork? }, duration in seconds), currentId, playing and onSelect(id). It is presentation only: you own the player, it owns the list. The current row is tinted, carries aria-current and says "Now playing" or "Paused" to a screen reader; four bars replace its number, move only while playing is true, rest at different heights when paused and stay still under reduced motion. Other rows show a play mark on hover and focus. Tab enters the list once, on the current item; the arrow keys, Home and End walk it; Enter calls onSelect, also for the current item (read it as play or pause). A cut title shows whole in a tooltip on hover and focus. showUpNext adds an "Up next" heading after the current item, kind="video" draws 16:9 thumbnails, title adds a header with count and total length, maxHeight sets where it scrolls, locale and labels translate. The list answers to its own width: below 24rem the numbers leave the rows (the current row shows its bars on its picture), pictures shrink and titles wrap to two lines (three below 20rem) instead of being cut to a few words; a video list always wraps to two.

items.name: media-playlist-demo
items.title: Media playlist demo
items.description: A working preview of Media playlist.

items.name: transcript-list
items.title: Transcript list
items.description: A synced transcript: each line with its timestamp, the spoken line highlighted, click to jump, and a search that marks the words it finds.
items.docs: Pass cues ({ start, end, speaker?, text }, seconds, from your own WebVTT parser), currentTime and onSeek. The line being spoken is highlighted and carries aria-current. While the media plays the list scrolls that line to a comfortable place, moving itself and never the page; if the reader scrolls it out of view, following stops and Jump to current appears, and it resumes when the line is back in view or the button is pressed. Timestamps are buttons that call onSeek(start); the text is plain, selectable text and clicking it seeks too, unless the click ended a selection. searchable (default true) adds a search that ignores case and accents, hides lines that do not match, marks the words that do and announces the count politely; defaultQuery and onQueryChange control it. A speaker name shows above each turn. autoScroll, maxHeight, locale and labels tune it.
