items.title: Transcript list demo
items.description: A working preview of Transcript list.

items.name: voice-message
items.title: Voice message
items.description: A chat voice note: play or pause, a waveform that fills as it plays and doubles as the seek slider, elapsed over total time, and a speed toggle.
items.docs: Pass src (an address or a data URI), peaks (loudness values on any scale), duration in seconds, sender ("me" sits right in the inverted tone, "them" left in the quiet one) and onPlay. The audio is fetched only as far as its length until play is pressed. The play button keeps its name and reports aria-pressed; the waveform is a slider (click or drag; arrow keys seek 5 seconds, 15 with Shift; Page Up and Down, Home and End) with its value written as "0:12 of 0:42". The speed button goes 1x, 1.5x, 2x. Starting one message pauses the one that was playing, through a tiny shared store (pauseAllPlayback() stops all), and a message that ends returns to its start. Loading shows a spinner and is announced; failure is written out ("Could not load voice message") with Try again. Without peaks a waveform is drawn from the address, the same on server and browser. name, defaultTime and labels tune it.

items.name: voice-message-demo
items.title: Voice message demo
items.description: A working preview of Voice message.

items.name: quiz-options
items.title: Quiz options
items.description: A multiple-choice question: pick one or several, lock it in, and every option is marked with an icon and a word, with a one-line reason.
items.docs: Pass question, options ({ value, label, reason? }) and correct (one value or a list). One right answer makes a radio group, several make checkboxes (multiple overrides). value (always a list), defaultValue and onValueChange control the choice. Check answer locks the question and marks every option that matters with an icon and a word, never colour alone: "Correct", "Your answer, incorrect", and for a right option left out "Missed" (several right) or "Correct answer" (one). A reason appears under its option once checked and is announced politely with the marks; the options stay focusable so a screen reader can walk the result. onCheck gets { correct, value }; the verdict panel is yours. status is controlled or kept inside; allowRetry turns the button into Try again, which clears the answer and calls onRetry. name submits one field per choice, labels translates.

items.name: quiz-options-demo
items.title: Quiz options demo
items.description: A working preview of Quiz options.

items.name: sentence-fields
items.title: Sentence fields
items.description: A rule written as a sentence with the choices inline: "Email me every Monday at 09:00 about new orders", for digests, alerts and automations.
items.docs: Pass template and slots. The template is an array of plain words, { slot: "id" } for a choice and { text: "at", withSlot: "time" } for words that come and go with a slot, or one string with {id} marks ("Email me {frequency} at {time}."). A slot has an id, options (strings or { value, label }), a placeholder, a label and an optional when ({ slot, is } or { slot, not }) that hides it, and its words, while the condition fails; a hidden slot keeps its answer. value, defaultValue and onValueChange hold the whole object by slot id. Each slot is the house select drawn as an underlined word (typeahead, arrow keys), and Tab walks the slots in reading order. The sentence is a group named by its own words, and a slot is named "Frequency: every Monday". A choice longer than the line wraps inside its slot, and a very long word is broken, so a phone never scrolls sideways. onSentenceChange gets { text, complete } for a confirmation step; sentenceText() (in sentence.ts) writes the same text anywhere, also on the server.

items.name: sentence-fields-demo
items.title: Sentence fields demo
items.description: A working preview of Sentence fields.

items.name: availability-grid
items.title: Availability grid
items.description: Paint the hours you are free: days across, hours down, drag or press to toggle, with a keyboard grid and a summary of the ranges.
items.docs: value is a list of slot keys: a day (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday), a dash and the start time, "1-09:00" for Monday from nine; onValueChange gets it sorted. days, weekStartsOn, startHour, endHour (the last row ends there) and slotMinutes (15, 20, 30, 60) shape the grid. Drag to paint a rectangle: the cell you start on decides, a chosen cell clears, an empty one fills; a day heading fills or clears its day; on touch a swipe still scrolls the page, and a finger that rests on a cell for a quarter of a second starts painting instead (the page stops scrolling under it and the card gets a ring). One tab stop: arrow keys move, Home, End, Page Up and Down jump, Space or Enter toggles, Shift with the arrows extends a range that Space applies. It is a grid role, each cell named and stated ("Tuesday 09:00 to 09:30, available"), changes announced politely. A summary folds the choice into ranges ("Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00") with hours a week. Chosen cells also carry a check in forced-colours mode. locale, hour12, name, labels.

items.name: availability-grid-demo
items.title: Availability grid demo
items.description: A working preview of Availability grid.

items.name: field-help-panel
items.title: Field help panel
items.description: A side panel of help that follows the field in focus: why we ask, an example and what happens next, beside the form on desktop and under the field on a phone.
items.docs: Pass help (field id to { title, body, example?, next?, link? }), the form as children and defaultId, the key of the general note. An element in the form with a data-help-id that is a key of help feeds the panel while the focus is in it: put it on the field or on the wrapper of its label, control and hint (FormField takes it as a prop). Below 1024px the help's bar goes last inside that element, so a wrapper wants a block or grid layout. On nothing with help the panel shows help[defaultId], which may be a field too. Changes cross-fade, instantly under reduced motion. Each field keeps its short hint in aria-describedby and the panel is a labelled complementary region, never a live region, so nothing depends on seeing it. Pin (aria-pressed) stops it changing while someone reads. From 1024px it is a sticky column (panelClassName moves where it sticks). Below that the column becomes two kinds of one-line bar: the general note above the form, and the help of the field in focus, put inside that field under its hint. Nothing above a field moves when it takes the focus, the bar stays under the last field you were in (also when the focus goes to a button), and a bar that is open stays open where it is when the focus moves on. A list that a field opens, a Select or a date picker, keeps the help on that field. In a row of fields give the row items-start, so an open bar does not stretch its neighbour. labels, headingLevel.

items.name: field-help-panel-demo
items.title: Field help panel demo
items.description: A working preview of Field help panel.

items.name: task-list
items.title: Task list
items.description: The hub of a long application: every section as a link with its status in words and a shape, a count of what is done, and a reason for what cannot start yet.
items.docs: Pass sections ({ id, title, href, status, hint }). status is completed, in-progress, not-started, needs-attention or cannot-start. The first four are links when they have an href, with the status as a pill: a disc with a check, a half-filled ring, a dashed ring, a disc with an exclamation mark. A section that cannot start is plain text with a lock and its hint, which is the reason, and has nothing to follow. The status and the hint are part of each link's accessible name ("Business details, In progress, 2 of 3 people added"). heading names the region and showSummary adds "3 of 6 sections complete" with a bar of one segment per section. onNavigate receives the section and the click event: call preventDefault to route it yourself. Rows are at least 56px tall; from 28rem of room the status becomes a column of its own. labels translates every word and locale writes the numbers.

items.name: task-list-demo
items.title: Task list demo
items.description: A working preview of Task list.

items.name: wizard-footer
items.title: Wizard footer
items.description: The Back, Skip and Continue bar of a multi-step flow: step context, a pending state that locks the other buttons, and the reason in words when Continue is off.
items.docs: Pass step (counted from 1), stepCount and onContinue. Back shows from step 2 when onBack is given. Skip shows when onSkip is given, so pass it only on optional steps. Continue says Next, or Finish on the last step; continueLabel overrides it. onContinue and onSkip may return a promise: that button shows a spinner and savingLabel while it runs, keeps the keyboard's focus (it is aria-disabled, never disabled) and the others lock; if it throws, the Error's message appears in a row of its own above the bar, as wide as the bar, and the step stays. While canContinue is false and canContinueReason is set, the reason replaces Continue as text in a polite live region. "Step 2 of 5" is a polite live region too, with a segment per step up to 8. sticky pins the bar to the bottom of the area that scrolls. The bar answers to its own width: under 28rem the buttons stack with Continue on top and a long label wraps, then they are a row, and from 36rem the step context joins that row. labels translates.

items.name: wizard-footer-demo
items.title: Wizard footer demo
items.description: A working preview of Wizard footer.

items.name: period-stepper
items.title: Period stepper
items.description: Step through days, weeks, months or years with previous, next and a Today shortcut. The label is announced as it changes, and the buttons switch off at your limits.
items.docs: unit is day, week (default), month or year. value is any day inside the period, written 2026-10-21; onChange receives the new period's first day and its { start, end, unit }. Days are calendar days, never moments, so nothing shifts with a time zone. min and max limit what can be shown: the buttons switch off at the period that holds the limit, and focus moves to the label so it is not lost. Today appears only when the period shown is not the current one and is within the limits. The label is a polite live region and a tab stop: with focus on it the left and right arrow keys step (reversed in right-to-left). Week labels read "Week 43, 19 to 25 Oct 2026" and day labels "Monday, 26 Oct 2026", both on two lines; weekStart 1 numbers by ISO, any other start counts the week holding 1 January as week 1. The control keeps the width of the widest label its unit can show in the language (a week across New Year, the longest month), so the buttons do not move as you step, and in a container too narrow for it the label shrinks and ends in an ellipsis. locale writes the label and timeZone decides what today is; a cached page must pass today or value. labels translates.

items.title: Question navigator
items.description: A numbered grid for quizzes and long forms: answered, flagged, current and open questions differ in shape and words, with a summary and one tap to jump.

A cell tells its state by shape: a dot for answered, a flag for flagged, an outline for the current one. Its name is one phrase: "Question 7, answered, flagged, current question". The summary above the grid ("Answered 14 of 20, 2 flagged") is a polite live region. The grid is one tab stop on the current cell; arrow keys move by a cell or a row, Home and End go to the ends of a row (with Control, to the first and last), Enter jumps. filter (all, unanswered, flagged) lists only those questions, set by you or with the buttons showFilter draws; an empty filter says so, and so does a list with no questions at all (labels.empty), instead of "Answered 0 of 0". columns is the most cells per row and a cell is never smaller than 2.5rem. showLegend draws the key. labels and locale translate.

items.name: environment-switcher
items.title: Environment switcher
items.description: Switch between Development, Staging and Production. The live one is drawn with a solid mark and the word Live, and asks for confirmation before you move to it.
items.docs: Pass environments ({ id, name, description, kind, consequence }), value and onValueChange (or defaultValue). kind is development, preview, staging or production, each with its own mark: an open ring, a dashed ring, a half-filled ring, a solid disc. Production is drawn as live on the button and in the list, with an inverted label that says Live, so it never depends on colour. The list is a menu of radio items with a check on the current one. confirmKinds (default: production) lists the kinds that ask first: an alert dialog names where you come from and where you go, says what changes (the environment's consequence, or a general sentence) and starts on Cancel. Cancel and Escape keep the current environment and return focus to the button. Any other kind switches at once. disabled turns the button off; align lines the list up with either edge. labels translates.

items.name: accordion-steps
items.title: Accordion steps
items.description: A multi-step form on one page: the current step is open, finished steps fold into a summary with Edit, later steps wait and say what must come first.
items.docs: Pass steps ({ id, title, content, state, summary, continueLabel }) and control current with onStepChange, or leave it uncontrolled. One step is open at a time; each reachable step is a button with aria-expanded inside a heading, in an ordered list. A complete step folds to its one-line summary (or renderSummary) with Edit, unless editable is false. Steps after the first incomplete one are locked and say "Complete Delivery first". Completion is yours, so editing a finished step never resets the steps after it. The open step that is not done is announced as "current step", the others as "not started", and a long title wraps. Opening a step moves focus to its heading button. onContinue may be async: Continue shows a pending state, keeps the keyboard's focus (it is aria-disabled, never disabled) and the other headers wait; if it throws an Error or returns a string, that message appears in the step, the step stays open and focus stays on Continue, otherwise the next step that is not complete opens. A step's content is mounted only while open, so keep field values in your own state. labels translates.

items.name: photo-select-grid
items.title: Photo select grid
items.description: Choose many photos from a library of hundreds: click or Space to toggle, Shift for a range, Ctrl A for all, with a live count and an optional limit.
items.docs: Pass photos ({ id, src, alt }) and the chosen ids as selected with onSelectedChange (or defaultSelected). Each photo is a checkbox named by its alt, with a circle that fills with a check. Click toggles; Shift-click chooses everything between the last photo you clicked and this one; Space toggles; Shift with an arrow key or Space extends a range (moving back takes the extra photos out); Control or Cmd with A chooses all; Escape clears. The grid is one tab stop and the arrow keys move like a grid. The status line ("3 selected") is a polite live region. maxSelect limits the choice: at the limit the others dim, the status line says "6 of 6 selected, limit reached" and a note under the grid says what to do. With onOpen, selecting starts with the first chosen photo: until then a plain click opens the photo and only the circle chooses it. Hundreds of photos are fine: tiles are memoised and pictures load lazily. Below 28rem of room the toolbar is two rows: the choice, the count and Clear, then your actions. columns, ratio, actions, labels, locale.

items.name: file-preview
items.title: File preview
items.description: Preview any file the right way: image, PDF, video, audio or text in place, with loading and failed states, an Open PDF fallback for phones and a Download for the rest.
items.docs: Pass file ({ name, mime, size, url, text, poster }). The type picks the renderer: an image fitted whole, a PDF in the browser's own viewer, video and audio with the native controls, a text or code file read in place when you give text, and for anything else its icon, name, size and a Download button. Nothing is fetched for you. maxHeight caps the preview (text scrolls, and is cut after 2,000 lines). Images, video, audio and PDFs have a loading and a failed state in words with Retry; a PDF counts as failed after 15 seconds. Where the browser has no PDF viewer (most phones) a message and an Open PDF link appear; embedPdf false forces that. status loading or failed (with onRetry) is for what you fetch yourself, like a file's text. onDownload turns Download into a button that calls you. The preview is a region named by the file's name and type. labels and locale translate.

items.name: branch-switcher
items.title: Branch switcher
items.description: Pick a branch or tag from a searchable popover: recent refs on top, matched letters in bold, a capped list for hundreds of refs, and Create branch from main.
items.docs: Pass branches (names), tags, recent (newest first, branches and tags together), value and onValueChange(name, kind), and defaultRef, the default branch: it is marked and listed first. The button shows the ref with an icon, and a long name gives way in the middle so its end stays readable. The popover has a search field and the Branches and Tags tabs, with a count on each that turns into the number of matches while typing. Matching ignores case; a name that holds the text whole beats scattered letters, initials work (fcr finds feature/checkout-redesign), and the letters that matched are bold. The list is a listbox driven from the search field: Arrow keys move, PageUp and PageDown jump, Enter chooses, and Escape empties the field before it closes the popover. Only the first pageSize refs (40) are drawn: Show more, or Arrow Down at the end, draws the next batch. The popover is never taller than the room the window has: the list gives way and the foot stays in reach, and Tab goes from the search field to the tabs and Show more, because the list is driven from the field and is no stop of its own. With onCreate(name, from), a typed name that is no branch yet gets a first row, Create branch feature/x from main; spaces become dashes, a name Git would refuse says why, the row shows a spinner while the promise runs, and a rejection keeps the popover open with its message. createFrom changes the base. When the name is found only in the other tab, a tag such as v2.3, the row is still there but not highlighted, so Enter does nothing until an arrow key chooses it, and a button under it, 3 in Tags, goes to the other tab. loading shows placeholders. BranchPanel (from the item's panel file) is the same list without the button, for a sheet on a phone; defaultQuery and autoFocus tune it. labels translates every word.

items.name: adaptive-nav
items.title: Adaptive nav
items.description: One list of destinations that is a bottom bar on a phone, a rail on a tablet and a sidebar on a desktop, chosen by its own width, with focus kept on the same item.
items.docs: Pass items ({ id, label, icon, href, badge, badgeLabel, group }), current (an id) and the page as children. The component measures its own width, not the window's, and follows the compact, medium and expanded window classes: below breakpoints.medium (600) it is a bar along the bottom, from there to breakpoints.expanded (840) a rail of icons with tooltips, and above that a sidebar with the groups as headings. Only one shape is in the page at a time, the current item carries aria-current in all of them, and when the shape changes focus goes to the same item in the new one. The bar shows the first four items and More, which opens a sheet inside the component with the rest, the header and the footer; five items and no header or footer fit without it. header and footer are the brand and the account: they fill the top and bottom of the sidebar and rail, and read the shape with useAdaptiveNavForm(), or with group-data-[form=rail]/adaptive-nav: classes. An item with an href is a link and an item without is a button; onNavigate(item, event) runs on a plain click, and a link is routed by you only when you call event.preventDefault(), so open-in-new-tab keeps working. A badge is a count or a short word, with badgeLabel to say what it counts. initialForm is the shape drawn on the server before the width is known. labels translates every word.

items.name: quick-exit
items.title: Quick exit
items.description: A quick exit for sensitive services: one button always in view, or Escape three times, blanks the page and replaces it with a neutral site.
items.docs: Put it first in your layout, so the first Tab reaches it, and pass href, the neutral site (required: pick one that is ordinary for your audience, a weather page or a news site). The button, Leave this site now by default (label), stays in a corner of the window (placement) on every page, 44px tall on a phone. Pressing it, or Escape three times within a second (shortcut, { key, presses, within } or false), blanks the page at once with a plain surface and nothing from your site on it, then replaces the current history entry with the neutral address (hideHistory, default true), so Back does not return, and opens it in the same tab. The button is named by what it says and described as Quick exit, opens a neutral site, with the shortcut added (labels). The Escape count ignores presses that came from inside a dialog, a menu or an open list, and presses that something already handled, so it never fights a dialog that closes on Escape; it counts in text fields, because someone typing a form must be able to leave. Each press shows on the button as Esc x3, x2, x1. onExit(event) runs a moment before the page goes, with the reason (button or keyboard) and the href: use it to clear a draft or a session, call event.preventDefault() to take over in a preview or a test, and keep analytics out of it. A browser still keeps its history and the page may show in an app switcher: say so on the page that explains how to stay safe.

items.name: go-to-shortcuts
items.title: Go-to shortcuts
items.description: Two-key navigation like G then I: press the prefix and a small panel lists where each letter goes, so the first press teaches the keys.
items.docs: Pass destinations ({ key, label, href, onGo }): onGo wins, and href loads the address. After the prefix (g by default) a hint panel appears at the bottom left of the window, listing each key with its label; the next key goes there, and Escape, any other key, a click or the timeout (1500 ms, shown as a bar running down along the foot of the panel) puts the panel away. The listener ignores presses in text fields, selects and editable areas, inside dialogs, with Ctrl, Cmd, Alt or Shift on the prefix, and while a key is held down. A screen reader hears Go to: press a letter, politely, and Going to Inbox after. scope is a ref to an element: only presses from inside it count, for a region of an app; leave it out to listen to the whole page. enabled turns it off. The panel is fixed, and className moves it, for example className="absolute bottom-3 left-3" inside a relative region. GoToHint is the same panel drawn on its own, to teach the keys in a help page. goToShortcut(key, prefix) from the item's shortcuts file returns { aria-keyshortcuts } for links you draw yourself: ARIA has no syntax for a sequence, so the value is the keys in order, g i. labels translates every word.

items.name: view-stack
items.title: View stack
items.description: Push and pop views inside one panel, like a phone settings app: titles, a Back button, a slide and a height that follows, in a popover, sheet or card.
items.docs: Pass views, a registry by id ({ settings: { title, content }, email: { … } }); the first is the root. defaultStack (ids, root first) or stack with onStackChange(stack) controls which are open. Each view has a heading; a view above another shows a Back button named after the title it returns to (labels.back, Back to {title}). A pushed view slides in from the side and the one below slides away, or they cross-fade under reduced motion; focus moves to the new heading, and on Back it returns to the row that opened the view. Views below the top stay mounted but are inert, so Tab and a screen reader only meet the one on top, and a form in them keeps what was typed. The height of the stack follows the view on top with a transition, so a popover or sheet resizes smoothly; give the stack a max-height class and a long view scrolls inside it with its header kept in place. Views push and pop with useViewStack(), which returns { stack, current, push(id, opener), pop(count), reset() }, or with ViewStackRow, a row with an icon, a name, what is set today and a chevron. headingLevel (2, 3 or 4) fits the headings to the page. The stack takes its background from its container (bg-inherit), so put a background on the popover, card or sheet around it.

items.name: filter-popover
items.title: Filter popover
items.description: A Filters button with a count that opens a panel of grouped options: choices are staged and applied together, with Reset and a live result count.
items.docs: Pass groups, each { id, label, kind } with kind checkbox or radio (options of { value, label, count, disabled }, and defaultValue for the option that means no filter), range ({ min, max, step, prefix, suffix }) or toggle ({ description }), value (the applied filters) and onApply(next), which receives only the groups that are on: checkbox lists of values, a radio value, a range as [min, max], a toggle as true. The button reads Filters with a badge counting the groups that are on, and opens a panel where every change is a draft: closing it with Escape or a click outside throws the draft away, and it starts from the applied value each time. Groups fold, the first and every group with something chosen start open, and a closed group says what is chosen in it. A checkbox or radio list with more than eight options gets a search field and scrolls inside itself, and in the popover Escape in that field empties it first and closes the panel only when it is already empty (a sheet around FilterPanel has to ask the same of its own Escape handler). A range is a slider with two number fields: a field takes what was typed when it is left or Enter is pressed, never a digit at a time, the smaller of the two numbers becomes the minimum, and an empty field leaves its end of the range open; the arrow keys and the spinner of a field step at once and stop at the other end of the range. Focus starts on the first group, not on Reset. Reset empties the draft and calls onReset; it stays focusable when it has nothing to do. The one button at the foot names what it will do: with resultCount(draft), sync or async, it counts as the draft changes (the first count at once, later ones after a short pause, late answers dropped) and says Show 128 results, Show results while the first count is on its way, and No results, switched off with a hint, when nothing would be left; without it, Apply 3 filters, Apply filters or Clear filters. Apply calls onApply when something changed, closes the panel, returns focus to the button and announces 3 filters applied in a live region that outlives the panel. At 320 pixels the panel stays inside the window and scrolls inside itself. trigger replaces the button, locale writes the numbers and plurals, and labels translates every word. FilterPanel (from the item's panel file) is the same panel without the popover, for a sheet on a phone.

items.name: notification-popover
items.title: Notification popover
items.description: The bell in a header: a count badge, a panel of the latest notifications with unread marked in words, mark all as read, and a link to the full list.
items.docs: Pass items (id, title, body, time, href, unread, actor or icon), the unreadCount if the server knows more than the list holds, and the callbacks: onOpenItem receives the event so a client-side router can call preventDefault, onMarkRead(id) runs for an unread row that was opened, onMarkAllRead shows the button. The badge caps at 99+ and the bell is named "Notifications, 3 unread"; the panel announces "3 unread notifications" when it opens from a live region on the bell. Rows are links (or buttons without an href) with one tab stop and arrow keys, Home and End between them. Pass now so the times, like "4 min. ago", are the same in server HTML and in the browser; without it they start as dates. NotificationPanel is the inside on its own, for a sheet on a phone. max is the most rows drawn, loading draws skeleton rows, and labels translate every word.

items.name: move-to-dialog
items.title: Move to dialog
items.description: Pick the destination folder for one or many items: a searchable tree, the current location marked, new folder inline and the path spelled out.
items.docs: Give folders as nested nodes ({ id, name, children, disabled, reason }), the currentFolderId, itemCount and mode ("move" or "copy"); onMove(folderId) may return a promise, and the dialog locks while it runs and closes when it resolves. The folder the items are in is marked Already here and cannot be chosen while moving; while copying it is marked Current folder and can be, because a copy may go beside its original. movingIds names the folders that are themselves being moved: they and everything inside them cannot be chosen, and each says why. A node with disabled and a reason cannot be chosen either. The search expands the matching branches; Enter in it chooses the first match. onCreateFolder(parentId, name) adds New folder, which puts a field under the selection; resolve with the new id or folder so it is chosen. The tree has a file manager's keyboard, and the chosen folder (or the one the items are in) is brought into view when it opens. On a narrow panel a folder that cannot be chosen gives its reason on a second line, whole. The foot spells the path out and the button names the folder. MoveToPanel is the inside on its own.

items.title: Duplicate dialog
items.description: Duplicate a project, document or board: a suggested name, checkboxes for what to copy with counts, and a link to the copy when it is ready.

The name starts as "Halcyon launch (copy)", or (copy 2) when that is taken, and a typed name that clashes is refused with a button that takes the nearest free one. onDuplicate({ name, include }) may return a promise: the fields lock and the button shows progress while it runs and the dialog will not close; resolve with the new item's address and the form is replaced by Copy created and an Open link, reject and the form stays as it was with the message above it and the button reads Try again. The foot says what will happen, "Copies 48 tasks and 12 files", from the counts and units. DuplicatePanel is the inside on its own.

items.name: find-in-page-bar
items.title: Find in page bar
items.description: Find text inside a document, log or article: a small bar with the match count, next and previous, and the matches marked in the text.
items.docs: Pass containerRef, the element whose text is searched, and put the bar inside a relative wrapper around it (not inside the element that scrolls), and leave room at the top of the region as high as the bar: two rows on a phone, so about 7rem. A bar that is open from the start (defaultOpen) takes no focus and scrolls nothing until somebody uses it. Matches are painted with the CSS Custom Highlight API where it exists, which leaves your elements alone, and with wrapper marks where it does not (highlight="marks" forces them); the marks are taken out again exactly. Marks are real changes to the page, so about 500 matches around the current one are marked at a time and the marks move along as you step; the count always covers every match. The current match is stronger and scrolled into view with room around it, the count reads "3 of 12" in a polite live region and "No results" when empty. Enter and Shift with Enter step, Escape closes, Ctrl or Cmd with F opens it while focus is inside the region (shortcut). Case and whole word are pressed buttons, controlled with caseSensitive, wholeWord and onOptionsChange. The text is read in idle slices, so a large log never stalls typing, and it is searched again if the region changes. onMatchesChange reports the count.

items.name: feedback-dialog
items.title: Feedback dialog
items.description: Collect product feedback in a small dialog: what kind it is, a message with a counter, an optional email and a thank-you that closes itself.

The counter shows only near maxLength and is read to screen readers at a few steps. askEmail is "optional", "required" or false. metadata, such as the page address, is listed in plain words before it is sent. Ctrl or Cmd with Enter sends. What was typed survives an accidental close. FeedbackPanel is the inside on its own.

items.name: newsletter-dialog
items.title: Newsletter dialog
items.description: A newsletter invitation that behaves: it opens after a delay or scroll depth, asks for one email, and stays away for weeks once dismissed.
items.docs: trigger is "delay" (delayMs, default 20 s), "scroll" (scrollDepth, a percentage) or "manual" (you control open). It never opens on the first page view of a session (pageViews, or its own count in sessionStorage, against minPageViews), never while somebody is typing in a field or another dialog is open, never in a background tab, and never again inside suppressDays after a dismissal or a sign-up. storage is a pair { read, write } for the moment of the last dismissal, so you choose cookie or localStorage (the default); read may return Infinity for someone who must never be asked. onDismiss says how: decline, close, escape or outside. onSubscribe(email) may return a promise; success replaces the form in place and closes after a moment. When it closes, focus returns to whatever had it when it opened, such as your own button with trigger="manual". incentive is the line about what people get. NewsletterPanel is the inside on its own.

items.name: external-link-dialog
items.title: External link dialog
items.description: The pause before leaving your site through a user-supplied link: it shows the real destination, says it is not yours, and offers Continue or Go back.
items.docs: Give it a trigger and an href for one link, or wrap content with intercept and every link inside that leaves your site asks first (your own origin, mailto, tel and trustedHosts pass through; a javascript or data link is stopped). A plain click is caught; a click with a modifier key goes through. The dialog says "This link goes to another website", shows the destination with the host in bold, and a host with look-alike letters is shown in its ASCII form under a warning, as is a user name hiding in front of the host. Continue is a real link that opens a new tab with noopener noreferrer, and Go back has focus; when the dialog closes, focus returns to the link or button that was clicked. The dialog never grows taller than the screen: it scrolls. trustedHosts match exactly or as *.example.com. onTrust(host) adds the Don't ask again for this site box, so you decide how to store it. onContinue and onCancel report the answer. ExternalLinkPanel is the inside on its own.

items.name: embed-dialog
items.title: Embed dialog
items.description: Let people embed your content: size and theme controls, a live code snippet that updates as they choose, and a copy button that confirms.
items.docs: buildSnippet(settings) returns the code for { width, height, theme, responsive }, and runs again on every change. embed-dialog/snippet exports escapeAttribute, which makes a value safe inside a double-quoted attribute (a quote or an ampersand cannot break out of it), and iframeSnippet, which writes an escaped iframe with lazy loading, the theme in the address, and for responsive a full-width wrapper that keeps the aspect ratio. controls picks which of width, height, theme and responsive to show. previewUrl (or a function of the settings) frames a page in a sandboxed frame of the same size (scripts run, but in an origin of their own; pass trustedPreview for a page of your own origin that needs its storage, and accept that such a page can lift its own sandbox), and preview draws it yourself; the frame is shrunk to fit and says by how much. With a preview the dialog is wider and the options sit beside it, so the code and its copy button stay in view. The code keeps its own lines and scrolls sideways when one is too long. The copy button confirms and is announced, and onCopy reports it. EmbedPanel is the inside on its own.

items.title: Event details popover
items.description: Click an event on a calendar to read it: title, time in the viewer's zone, place, people and actions, in a panel anchored to the chip.
items.docs: Pass event and the event chip as children: the chip opens the panel. viewerTimeZone is the reader's own IANA zone; when its clock differs from the event's, both are written, each with the name of its zone. A cancelled event has its title struck through and says Cancelled, a tentative one says so, one that is on says Happening now and one that is over says how long ago (pass now for the same text on the server and in the browser). A long description is cut to four lines with a Show more button that appears only when something is hidden. actions takes your own Buttons for the foot. The popover is non-modal: Escape or a click outside closes it and focus goes back to the chip. The panel is never taller than the room there is: on a short screen it scrolls inside itself and its close button stays in view. EventDetailsPanel is the same content without the popover, for a side panel or a sheet.

items.title: Template picker dialog
items.description: Start from a template: a dialog with search, categories, a grid of cards, a preview of the one in focus and Blank always first.
items.docs: Pass templates ({ id, name, description, category, preview, tags }) and categories ({ id, label }). The preview is any node that fills its box, such as an SVG with a viewBox, because it is drawn small on the card and larger beside the grid. onSelect receives the template id, or null for Blank, which is always the first card and the default. Return a promise and the dialog locks while it runs, cannot be closed and closes when it resolves; if it rejects, it stays open and says why. The arrow keys move across the grid and choose, Enter makes it, and Escape empties a search before it closes the dialog. Below 640px the side panel becomes a sheet at the foot. What is chosen is always in the grid: a pick that a search or a category hides is set aside and Blank stands in until the filter lets go of it, and a search that finds nothing in the open category says where the matches are and offers Search all templates. TemplatePickerPanel is the inside of the dialog, for a page of its own. labels translates every word.

items.name: recommendation-reason-popover
items.title: Recommendation reason popover
items.description: Answer why am I seeing this next to a recommendation or ad: the reasons in plain words, and one-step controls to see less of it.
items.docs: Pass reasons ({ label, detail, kind }) in plain language, most important first, and sponsored ({ by, note }) for an ad: it says so before anything else and names who paid. onLessLikeThis and onHide add real buttons; return a promise and the row spins, then confirms in its own place (We will show you less like this), and if it rejects the row goes back and says why. settingsHref adds the link to your personalisation settings. trigger replaces the small info button, which is named Why am I seeing this? (title changes both). The panel is a non-modal popover, so it works with touch, keyboard and screen readers, and Escape returns focus to the button. On a short screen the panel scrolls inside itself and its close button stays in view. RecommendationReasonPanel is the same content without the popover. labels translates every word.

items.title: Document stats popover
items.description: Words, characters, sentences and reading time for a document or the current selection, with an optional goal, from the editor footer.
items.docs: Pass text, and selectionText while something is selected: the button reads 412 words (or 36 of 412 words) and the panel shows words, characters with and without spaces, sentences, paragraphs and the time to read and to say it aloud, tagged Document or Selection. Words and sentences are counted by the rules of the locale. goal adds a bar and Goal: 800 words, 388 to go. A text over 20,000 characters is counted in idle time, so typing never waits for it, and a screen reader hears the new count only once typing has paused. wordsPerMinute and speakingWordsPerMinute set the pace. trigger replaces the button. The panel is never taller than the room there is; on a short screen it scrolls inside itself. countText, in the item's stats file, counts a text for DocumentStatsPanel when you use the panel alone.

items.name: props-table
items.title: Props table
items.description: An API reference table for docs: name, type, default, required and description, with nested object props that expand.
items.docs: Pass rows ({ name, type, defaultValue, required, description, children, group }). A union type breaks at its pipes, a required prop carries the word Required and a prop with no default says None. A row with children has a button that opens its fields beneath it, indented, to any depth; defaultExpanded opens some at the start. Every row has an id (prop-variant, or data-table-variant with idPrefix) and a link: opening the page at one opens what holds it, scrolls there and highlights the row. Below 42rem of width each prop becomes a block with its name on top, and the rows keep their table semantics for screen readers. labels translates every word.

items.name: timesheet-grid
items.title: Timesheet grid
items.description: A weekly timesheet: projects down, days across, hours in each cell, with row and day totals, a daily target and week navigation.
items.docs: Pass projects ({ id, name, client }) and entries as entries[projectId]["2026-10-26"] = 7.5, with onChange(entries, change) to keep them; weekStart with onWeekChange, or defaultWeekStart, sets the week. A cell reads 7.5, 7:30, 7h 30m or 90m. Enter saves and moves down, the arrow keys move between cells, Escape undoes, and what cannot be read is said in words and kept to fix: every cell that was refused stays marked until it is edited, saved or undone. Row totals sit at the end and day totals in the footer; with dailyTarget and dailyCap a day says Target met, how much is short or to go, or that it is over the cap, always in words. Today's column says Today (pass now for the same output on the server and in the browser). locked makes every cell read-only and shows lockedReason. format switches between 7.5 and 7:30. On a phone the week scrolls sideways beside the pinned project names, a soft shade at the right edge says there is more, and the hint speaks of touch. labels translates every word.

items.name: attendance-register
items.title: Attendance register
items.description: A register of who came: people down the side, sessions across, a present, late, absent or excused mark per cell and a rate per person.
items.docs: Pass people, sessions ({ id, date, title }) and marks as marks[personId][sessionId] = "late", with onMarkChange(changes, marks) to keep them. Every mark is a glyph and a word, and each cell is named in full (Mara Visser, 12 Oct, late). A cell opens a menu of present, late, absent and excused; with the keyboard the arrow keys move across the grid, P, L, A and E set a mark and Backspace clears it. Each row ends with a rate (the sessions someone came to, of those that count: excused and unmarked ones are left out), the footer counts who came, and a button in a session's heading marks everyone who has no mark yet as present. A cell that still needs a mark shows a dashed outline and a plus, so what is left to mark is seen without pointing. A session after today is disabled and says why (pass now for stable output). readOnly shows plain marks. labels translates every word.

items.name: access-level-menu
items.title: Access level menu
items.description: The role control beside a person or a link: one choice of access levels with a line on what each allows, levels you cannot grant explained, and Remove access kept apart.
items.docs: Pass levels ({ id, label, description }) and either value with onValueChange or a defaultValue. onValueChange(id) may return a promise: the button shows the choice and a spinner while it runs, and if it rejects the button goes back to the level it had and writes the reason under itself (an Error's message is added to the sentence). disabledLevels ({ id, reason }) keeps a level the person may not be given in the list with its reason under it; it stays reachable with the arrow keys so the reason is read, and choosing it does nothing. onRemove adds a destructive entry below a separator (removeLabel renames it), and confirmRemove turns the menu into 'Remove access? Yes, remove access / Keep access' first, with focus on the safe answer. locked shows the level as text with a lock and lockedReason beneath it, for an owner row. subject names the button for a screen reader ('Access for Dana Whitfield: Editor'), size is sm or default, variant is outline or ghost, and every change, removal and refusal is said in a polite live region. align picks the edge the menu lines up with and the edge a message under the button hangs from, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the menu, and a menu that is open from the start never takes focus from the page. labels translates every word.

items.name: role-change-dialog
items.title: Role change dialog
items.description: Confirm a role change by showing what the person gains and loses in plain words, and ask for the email to be typed before anyone is made an owner.
items.docs: Pass member ({ name, email, image }), fromRole and toRole ({ id, name, capabilities, powerful }) and onConfirm. Every role lists everything it allows (a string, or { id, label }), and the dialog works out Gains and Loses from the two lists, with a count of what stays the same, so the change reads right however many roles you have. The two lists sit side by side once the panel is 28rem wide and both have something to show; a side with nothing on it is one quiet line across the full width. onConfirm({ member, fromRole, toRole }) may return a promise: the field locks, the button shows progress and the dialog will not close; on success the form becomes 'Role changed' and 'Dana Whitfield now has the Editor role.' with focus on Done when the focus was in the panel (a panel that nobody pressed by hand never takes focus or scrolls the page), and on a rejection the form stays with the Error's message above the buttons and the button says Try again. warnOnDowngrade (default true) adds a note when something is taken away. A toRole with powerful: true asks for the member's email (their name when there is none) to be typed, and the button stays off until it matches. lastOwner refuses a change that takes something away and says why; blockedReason refuses any other change in your own words; two roles that allow the same say so. It is an alert dialog, so focus starts on Cancel: trigger is the element that opens it, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control it, and RoleChangePanel is the inside on its own (standalone). labels translates every word and locale the counts.

items.name: request-access-dialog
items.title: Request access dialog
items.description: For someone who lands on something they cannot open: ask the owner for access with an optional note, then see that it was sent and what happens next.
items.docs: Pass resourceName, owner ({ name, email, image }), levels ({ id, label, description }; with a single level the choice is left out), onRequest({ level, message }) and, when you know it, signedInAs, which says as whom the person is asking and where the answer will go. onRequest may return a promise: the fields lock, the button shows progress and the dialog will not close; on success the form becomes 'Request sent to Maya Okafor' with what happens next and focus on Close when the focus was in the panel (a panel that nobody pressed by hand never takes focus or scrolls the page), and on a rejection the form stays with the note still in it and the Error's message above the buttons. pendingSince (a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp) recognises a repeat request: a notice reads 'Already requested 2 hours ago' and the button offers Send again. Pass now to get those words in server HTML, otherwise they appear once the browser's clock is read; locale and timeZone shape the words and the dates. maxLength limits the note (default 280, counted by the textarea counter), showOwnerEmail adds the owner's address (off by default: it is theirs to share), and Ctrl or Command with Enter sends from the note. trigger is the element that opens the dialog, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control it, RequestAccessPanel is the inside on its own (standalone), and labels translates every word.

items.name: display-options-popover
items.title: Display options popover
items.description: The Display button of a list view: choose layout, grouping, ordering and which properties show, with changes applying at once and a reset.
items.docs: Pass layouts ({ id, label, icon }), groupings and orderings ({ id, label }), properties ({ id, label, visible }) and the current value ({ layout, grouping, ordering, direction, properties }) with onValueChange, or a defaultValue to let the popover keep it. Layout is a group of small icon tiles (a list, board, table, grid or calendar id draws its own icon, and icon replaces it); grouping and ordering use the house select, with a button that turns the ordering round; properties are chips that show and hide fields, and value.properties holds the ids that show. Every change applies at once through onValueChange(next). The button counts how many of the four settings differ from the defaults (ordering counts once, whether the field or the direction moved) and is named 'Display, 2 changed'; the defaults are the first layout, grouping and ordering, ascending, and the properties not marked visible: false, or pass defaults. Reset puts the defaults back, calls onReset and says 'Back to the defaults' in a polite live region. A saved value that names an option that no longer exists falls back to the default for it. The panel keeps inside the window and scrolls inside itself at 320 pixels. trigger replaces the button, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the panel, DisplayOptionsPanel is the inside on its own for a sheet on a phone, and labels translates every word.

items.name: recent-items-popover
items.title: Recent items popover
items.description: A Recent button that lists what you opened lately, grouped by day, with pinning and a Clear history that offers Undo instead of asking, for apps where people jump around.
items.docs: Pass items ({ id, title, kind, href, openedAt, pinned }) in any order; the panel groups them under Pinned, Today, Yesterday and Earlier and orders each group newest first. kind picks the icon and the word under the title (project, document, record, board, folder, file, sheet and image are known, labels.kinds adds more). Pass now and timeZone so the headings and the times ('12 min. ago') are the same in server HTML and in the browser, with locale for the words; without now the browser's clock is read once the page is live. max is how many unpinned items are listed (default 8). Rows are links, or buttons without an href: onOpen(item, event) receives the event so a client-side router can preventDefault, and the popover closes. The list has one tab stop, the arrow keys, Home and End move between rows, Enter opens one and P calls onPin(item, pinned); a pin button on each row does the same for a pointer, and focus follows the item to its new group. onClear shows Clear history: the rows disappear and an Undo bar runs for undoMs (6 seconds), and only when Undo goes unused is onClear(clearedItems) called, which is the moment to delete them and to remove them from items; pinned items are kept, and closing the popover ends the wait. With nothing to show the panel explains that recent items appear after opening something. RecentItemsPanel is the inside on its own, trigger replaces the button, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the popover, and labels translates every word.

items.name: avatar-group-popover
items.title: Avatar group popover
items.description: Make the +5 on an avatar stack useful: press it to see everyone in a short list with name, role and presence, and filter when the list is long.
items.docs: Pass people ({ id, name, role, image, status }) in the order the stack should show them, and max (default 4): that many avatars are drawn, and the rest fold into a button named 'Show 5 more people' that opens the list of everyone; with no more people than max there is no button. Each visible avatar is an image with the person's name, and the whole stack is a group that reads as 'Maya Okafor and 6 others' ('A and B' for two). The list shows an avatar, the name, the role in muted text and the presence as a drawing and a word (online, away, busy, offline: a disc, a half disc, a ring with a bar, a ring), never colour alone. It is one tab stop with the arrow keys, Home and End, and it scrolls inside itself when it is long. searchable (default true) adds a filter field once there are more than eight people: Escape empties it before it closes the list, the arrow down goes to the first row, names are matched without capitals and accents, and a polite line says how many match. onSelect(person) makes the rows buttons and closes the list; without it the rows are plain text. viewAllHref adds a link at the foot, size is sm, default or lg, align picks the edge, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the list, locale shapes the counts, and labels translates every word.

items.name: snooze-popover
items.title: Snooze popover
items.description: Snooze until later: presets for this evening, tomorrow and next week worked out from now, plus a date and time of your own, with the zone said aloud.
items.docs: Pass onSnooze(date), the moment of the choice, and a now, a timeZone and a locale: every choice is worked out from now on the calendar of that zone through Intl (never the zone of the machine, daylight saving included), so the server and the browser agree; without now the browser's clock is read once the page is live. The four default choices are Later today (18:00), Tomorrow morning (08:00), This weekend (Saturday 09:00, not offered on a Sunday) and Next week (Monday 08:00), each with the day and the time at the right ('Tomorrow, 08:00', 'Sat 24 Oct, 09:00'), and a choice that would land in the past is left out. Pass presets ({ id, label, resolve(now, timeZone) }) to replace them: resolve returns a Date, or null when the choice does not apply, and atTime and nextWeekday in snooze.ts do the zone work. 'Pick date and time' opens the Calendar and a time field (the house select, in half hours, written the way the locale writes a time), writes the choice out in words ('Snooze until Thu 23 Oct, 08:00') and refuses a time that has passed, so the slots that have gone are off for today; the zone is said in full words at the foot. onSnooze may return a promise: the row shows progress, and a rejection keeps the panel open with a message. A choice closes the popover and is announced from the button ('Snoozed until Thu 23 Oct, 08:00'). The list is one tab stop with the arrow keys, and Enter on a choice snoozes it; in the calendar view Enter on the Snooze button, or Ctrl or Command with Enter from anywhere in it, confirms. trigger replaces the button, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the popover, SnoozePanel is the inside on its own, and labels translates every word.

items.name: local-time-popover
items.title: Local time popover
items.description: Show an event time in everyone's time zone: a popover from the time itself lists the same moment in your zone and the zones you choose.
items.docs: Pass instant (an ISO string with its offset, or a Z), zones ({ id, label }; the id is an IANA name such as America/Los_Angeles) and, as you need them, eventZone (default: the first zone), viewerZone, locale, format, now and title. The trigger is a button holding a real time element written in the event's zone, by default as '17:00 CET', or as you say with format (Intl.DateTimeFormat options). Pressing it opens the same moment in each zone, the viewer's own zone first and tagged 'You' (added at the top if it is not among zones, and read from the browser when viewerZone is not given: nothing depends on the server's zone), each with the time, the date, the distance from UTC in tabular digits ('UTC+1', 'UTC−7', 'UTC+5:30') and 'Next day' or 'Previous day' where the date differs from the event's. Offsets and dates are worked out for the actual date by Intl, so daylight saving is right on both sides of a change of clocks. The head of the list gives the event's day and, measured from now (pass it for server HTML), 'in 5 days'. Copy as text puts one line on the clipboard ('Halcyon product sync: Mon 26 Oct, 17:00 Amsterdam (UTC+1) / 09:00 San Francisco (UTC−7) / ...', with a date where a zone is on another day) and says Copied. align, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the popover, LocalTimePanel is the inside on its own, and labels translates every word.

items.name: route-timetable
items.title: Route timetable
items.description: A line's timetable as a real table: stops down the side, trips across, the next departure marked in words, and on a phone a stop picker with that stop's times.
items.docs: Pass stops ({ id, name, note }) in route order and trips ({ id, label, note, times }), where times is an object of 24-hour clock times by stop id: { harbour: "08:00", marina: "08:12" }. A stop that is left out, or null, is one the trip does not stop at: the cell shows a dash and says 'does not stop'. now decides which trip is next and which have gone; leave it out to use the browser's clock (read after the page is live, then every half minute) or pass it to get the same page on the server and in tests. Times are read in timeZone (default UTC) and written in locale (default en-US, so '7:42 AM'; en-GB writes '07:42'). The reader picks their stop in the picker above the grid: pass highlightStop with onHighlightStopChange to control it, or defaultHighlightStop to start somewhere. The next trip at that stop is marked 'Next', trips that have left it are muted, and a line says how long to wait. The grid opens scrolled to the next trip and follows when another stop is picked, but never moves by itself as time passes. The stop column stays pinned and the scroll box takes the keyboard. In a box narrower than 36rem the grid is replaced by the picker and the list of that stop's times, with the caption above the picker. There everything before the last trip that left folds into one line to open: that trip stays, as context, and a run that skips the stop is folded with the rest. caption names the table, note goes under it, and labels translates every word, including the line shown when there are no stops or trips.

items.name: departures-board
items.title: Departures board
items.description: A departures board for stations, ferries and airports: time, destination, platform and a status in words, delays shown against the plan, changes announced politely.
items.docs: Pass departures ({ id, scheduled, expected, destination, via, platform, status, operator }) in any order; the board sorts them by the time they leave. scheduled and expected are ISO strings with their offset (or Z), timestamps or Dates, because the board has to know the day to know what has left. A delay is worked out from the two times and shown as the planned time struck through beside the new one; give status 'cancelled' or 'boarding' to say those, 'on-time' or 'delayed' to override the sum. now decides which rows have left (they fade back and say 'Departed'); leave it out to use the browser's clock, or pass it for the same page on the server and in tests. updated sets the 'Updated 14:32' stamp (default: now). Times are written in locale (default en-US; en-GB writes 14:35) in timeZone (default UTC; a zone that is not known falls back to UTC). Give departures a new array whenever the data updates: the rows that changed rest on a plate for a moment, and a polite live region says what changed in one sentence for the first three rows (cancellations first, then delays, boarding and platforms), gathered so a burst of updates is never a flood; the first paint says nothing. onSelect makes each destination a button. labels translates every word, and platform can be renamed Gate, Pier or Stand. Below 42rem each row is a card of two lines, or three when the stops and the operator do not fit beside the status, and they wrap instead of being cut off.

items.name: standings-table
items.title: Standings table
items.description: A league table: position, club, played, won, drawn, lost, goal difference and points, with form shapes and promotion and relegation zones named in words, not colour.
items.docs: Pass rows in table order: { team, logo, position, played, won, drawn, lost, for, against, points, form }. Position defaults to the place in rows, so rows that are already in order need none. Points are never worked out, because the rules differ; goal difference is for minus against and always shows its sign. form is the last results, oldest first, as 'WWDLW', ['W','D'] or the words win, draw and loss: the last five are drawn as a filled shape for a win, a hollow one for a draw and a dash for a loss, and read out as 'Last five: win, win, draw, loss, win'. zones ({ from, to, label, tone }) put a rule on the left of their rows (solid for positive, dashed for neutral, dotted and destructive for negative) and a line in the legend; a screen reader hears the zone after the club's name. highlightTeam names a club to single out with a star, a plate and the word 'highlighted'. The columns step aside as the box narrows, down to position, club, played and points, by container width and not by screen, and the crest steps aside below 22rem so a club's name is never clipped. It renders on the server. locale writes the figures and labels translates every word, including the column abbreviations and their full forms.

items.name: competition-results-table
items.title: Competition results table
items.description: Results of a race or competition by category: place, athlete, club, finish time and gap to the winner, with ties, records and non-finishers named in words.
items.docs: Pass results ({ place, name, club, bib, category, time, status, marks, note }) in any order and categories ({ id, label }) for the tabs; a result's category is the id of one of them. time is seconds or text such as '1:02:45', '20:15.4' or '58.42', and is written the way a results sheet writes it (with hours once any time needs them) and read out in words. Places come from the times, and athletes with the same time share a place and are marked 'equal'; give every finisher an official place and the table trusts those instead (a photo finish, a penalty). A category tab narrows the table and counts the places again inside it; control it with category and onCategoryChange, or start it with defaultCategory. An entry with status 'dnf', 'dns' or 'dsq', or with no time, says 'Did not finish', 'Did not start' or 'Disqualified' in words and is kept below the finishers. marks ('record', 'personal-best', 'season-best') become labelled badges by the name. highlightName marks an athlete with a plate and the word 'You'. precision (0, 1 or 2) sets the digits after the second. onSelect makes each name a button. Below 48rem club, category and bib fold under the name, and below 28rem the gap folds under the time. The folded bib is written by labels.bibFolded ('#{bib}' by default; 'Lane {bib}' for a pool). labels translates every word.

items.name: design-token-table
items.title: Design token table
items.description: Design tokens documented as a table: each drawn as itself, with its value and a copy button, a filter that marks matches, folding groups and a link per token.
items.docs: Pass tokens ({ name, value, type, usage, group, contrast }) where type is color, size, radius, shadow, font or duration. The preview draws the value itself: a swatch (over a checkerboard when it is see-through), a bar as long as a length, a corner for a radius, a raised tile for a shadow, a font specimen, and for a duration a track that grows with the time (a second is the whole width) with a dot that runs along it for that long when the row is hovered or has focus (under reduced motion it stays put). The value is mono with a copy button. Groups fold (defaultFolded names the ones that start folded), and the filter matches name or value, marks what matched and opens every group that has a match. Each name links to its own row (idPrefix goes before every anchor when two tables share a page); a link to a token inside a folded group opens the group and scrolls to the token. Name a colour token in background and every colour shows its WCAG contrast against it as a ratio and a grade in words with a glyph; a colour the table cannot read (hsl, a name, a var) shows none, and contrast: false leaves one out. Narrower than 56rem the table becomes one card per token. onCopy is called after a copy and labels translates every word.
